News.title: Chilling footage shows serial sexual predator Simon Levy leading murder victim to her death and stalking women on street
News.content:
CHILLING footage shows serial sexual predator Simon Levy leading one of his murder victims to her death and stalking women on the street.

Catastrophic blunders in the system left the vile offender free to kill two sex workers after raping a third – while he was on bail for string of sexual assaults.



Levy, 40, embarked on a shocking rampage where he murdered two women, left another for dead and sexually assaulted ten young women on the London Underground weeks after being freed from prison in September 2024.

He was released after serving a three year sentence for molesting two women in public, and subject to a sexual offenders’ order in which he was meant to be watched closely by authorities.



Harrowing footage shows the monster in the streets and on the Tube where he prowled for victims, as well as the moment he led a woman to her death.

CCTV videos also show Levy getting off the bus at High Court road in Tottenham, north London, before he murdered his second victim Sheryl Wilkins on August 24 2025.



A body worn camera videos show the moment the vile attacker is arrested on suspicion of murder – and again for the second and final time five months later.

Levy was jailed in 2021 for sexual assaults, and carried on preying on woman after he was released in 2023.

In a separate trial, he was convicted of 11 counts of sexual assault in which ten of the victims were young women who were using the Tube, and the 11th was a prison officer, assaulted while he was behind bars in 2022.

In January 2025, Levy strangled a woman unconscious before raping her in a car park and leaving her “as good as dead”.

The surviving victim had told cops that she had been raped and knew where her attacker lived, but she was not formally interviewed until after he had killed twice.



In March 2025, he killed Carmenza Valencia Trujillo, 54, before dumping her body in the stairwell of a derelict building in Peckham, South East London – all while still on bail.

Levy – who had a “compulsive or pathological desire to assault women” – was one of seven arrested over her murder, but was released under investigation on April 1 – leaving him free to murder his third victim.

Sheryl Wilkins, 39, was found dead near a B&M store in Tottenham in late August of the same year, just two days after Levy failed to appear at court.



Chilling footage shows Levy and Wilkins walk through the car park where she was murdered.

Yesterday, the “predatory monster” was found guilty of two counts of rape, two of murder, one of GBH and one of intentional suffocation.

Police and prosecutors faced questions for failing to stop the half blind serial attacker in his tracks.

In a shocking “systematic failure”, the court heard Levy had been carrying out daily attacks for years, with dozens more potential victims out there as cops urge them to come forward.

The unemployed loner, who lived with his mum in Tottenham, was separately found guilty earlier this year of sexually assaulting ten women on London’s Tube network over a 19-month period.



Cops have urged more victims of Levy’s to come forward, as London’s victims’ commissioner said a “litany of failures” had allowed him to commit his heinous crimes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Independent Office of Police Conduct (IOPC) confirmed two officers are being investigated over their handling of Levy.

The Metropolitan Police, British Transport Police and Crown Prosecution Service have all admitted to failures in how the brute was monitored between his first conviction and his arrest for murder.

News.title: Meet the Brit dads who were hunted down & now pay for kids they abandoned overseas – as time’s up for rest to be exposed
News.content:
BABIES born to British ‘sex tourists’ and poverty-stricken women in the Philippines are being abandoned by their British fathers – but time is running out for them.

In an exclusive series – Looking for Dad: The Children of Britain’s Sex Tourists – we reveal how errant dads are being hunted down as a revolutionary organisation uses DNA to track them down and make them pay for their desperate children.



READ PART ONE OF OUR EXPLOSIVE NEW SERIES, LOOKING FOR DAD: THE CHILDREN OF BRITAIN’S SEX TOURISTS

READ PART TWO OF OUR EXPLOSIVE NEW SERIES, LOOKING FOR DAD: THE CHILDREN OF BRITAIN’S SEX TOURISTS



But of course, not every British dad fathered a child through a sex worker – or chose to walk away.

Journalist and charity worker Margaret Simons tells how some families made it work.

JUST before Christmas, identical twins Madeline and Melanie delos Santos met their father for the first time in 22 years.

The 25-year-olds had spent decades desperate for a relationship with their British dad, a retired civil engineer.

I head a charity that helped track down their father. But contact was sparse after our investigators tracked him down.

Then, out of the blue, he told them he was coming to Angeles and wanted to see them.



They arranged to meet at his hotel for breakfast. Madeline says she walked into the room, saw her father’s back and recognised him straight away, even though she hadn’t seen him since she was a toddler.

She says: “In that moment I realised I did need him, though I had told myself I didn’t. I realised that I am now complete. And all of the questions, all of my anger and hatred towards him, all of it vanished in a second. It was all gone.”

Why had their dad, who we will name Roy, chosen this moment to visit? The twins don’t know. Says Melanie: “Maybe because he’s old. Maybe he realised it is his responsibility to show up.”

Twenty-five years ago, Roy was working in the Philippines and met Esperanza delos Santos, or Espy as she is known to her family, in a bar on Fields Avenue. He fell for her.

When he was transferred to Bali, Espy moved with him. She returned home when she was seven months pregnant and gave birth to the twins. The family has a faded picture of the Christening, with Roy holding one of the babies.



But then, when the children were still toddlers, the relationship failed, and Roy left.

The family tell me that, to start with, he sent money each month. He provided them with a letter confirming the twins were his children and consenting to them using his family name.

Then, on his retirement, he made one last payment – 1.5 million pesos, (£21,000), with the instruction that it be used to buy a house for his girls.

Roy gave what he thought was fair. It is more than many fathers do. But what he gave is also almost certainly much less than he would have had to give, by law, had his daughters been born in Britain.

The girls were raised by their extended family, and in particular their grandmother, the family matriarch. They were able to attend a private school and gain a decent education, thanks to an uncle sending home remittances from his job as a waiter in Dubai.



But underlying the family say there was a hurt and abandonment.

When the twins were 11, their grandmother allegedly wrote to Roy asking for more money to pay school fees. She says he wrote back that he had no job and no income.

A letter seen by The Sun reads: “We cannot avoid a difficult decision to make about the twins. With both of us without money and still some years to go before they are independent, the only option I can think of is adoption. I hate to say [this] but what else can we do?”



I first met Melanie and Madeline in 2018, just after they turned eighteen. They were gorgeous – smart, thoughtful and kind. But lack of money meant they had to abandon their education and seek work.

All the girls wanted was to know their father. They weren’t after his money.

At the twins’ request, the charity I run tracked down Roy, who was living a middle-class life in the Home Counties, and rang him to tell him about his daughters’ request.

After a few days and some emails, he rang the girls, and they had a good conversation and agreed to keep in touch. But the contact proved sporadic. It was always the girls seeking him, tracking him. He never initiated contact – until last year.

After I wrote about the twins several years ago, Madeline was sponsored by an architect who read my article.



This good samaritan paid her university fees, and last year she graduated as an architect, and now works for an Angeles City architectural firm.

Melanie has a job as a marketing assistant for a motorcycle dealer.

And then their father came to visit. Roy spent three days in Angeles City, and the girls spent as much time with him as they could, sharing every meal.

He met their mother again. That was bittersweet. He did not recognise her.

For the girls, it was a revelation. They noticed mannerisms and habits of thought they had in common. They share his chin. Madeline recognised that “we share a certain way of thinking. A mindset.”



He gave them an explanation, of sorts, for why he had left them behind as tiny children. The girls have asked that the details be kept confidential for their mother’s sake.

Madeline said: “He has a point. I don’t agree with what he did, but I understand better.”

Nevertheless, she has a message for British fathers of Filipino children: “Have a sense of responsibility. Don’t hide your children, because it’s important for them to be proud of themselves and to know who they are.”

And to the many other children of British fathers, she says: “Don’t lose hope. You are worth something just by yourself. And one day you may find your father.”

Thankfully, not all British men who have children in the Philippines abandon them.



David, now 69, who has asked us not to use his surname, first came to the Philippines in 1981 when he was working for a resources trading company.

David did not pay for sex.

He married a Filipino he met while working in South Asia, but they broke up.

Over the years, he travelled back and forth to the Philippines, and when he was in his early 40s met 27 year old Jessica Gutierrez, a waitress at a backpacker restaurant, who became his girlfriend.



He stayed with her for over a year, ending up managing the restaurant in which she worked.

Then she told him she was carrying his child. Their relationship had ended, and she was assuming he would abandon them and go back to London.

David knew that was all too common a scenario, but he wanted to be different.

“I decided I wouldn’t go that route,” he said. “I was in my early 40s. I didn’t have a kid. My brother didn’t have kids.



“There was just something in me that said, ‘I want this. It is the right thing.’”

He asked for and obtained a DNA test to confirm the child was his, and committed to supporting him come what may.

His son William Gutierrez was born in 2000. By now, David was working in the UK, but visited about every eighteen months, and paid to support William.

His mother helped as well and brought birthday and Christmas gifts for the grandchild she had never met in person.

David says: “I didn’t know him very well when he was a young kid, which I think actually was an advantage because, put it this way, women are far better with young children than men are. That’s a biological fact. So I missed the toddler tantrums and the nappies and everything like that.”



But he paid for private schools and medical needs, sending money whenever it was needed – he estimates the cost of around £250 per month.

Then, in 2019, he got a job in Manila running a call centre and began to get to know his son. It was life-affirming.

William, now 25, recently graduated as an electrical engineer. He lives in Cebu, and the two men meet frequently.

David says: “I visit. We go to bars, we drink beer and watch football. We are great friends.”

Now retired, David divides his time between the Philippines and the UK, always trying to avoid the “horrible” British winter.



But the main reason he spends so much time here is his son. “He is a great man, feet on the ground,” David says. “The best thing I ever did. I am very proud of him.

“If it wasn’t for him, I would probably come every couple of years just to see friends for two or three weeks, and that would be it.”

What does he have to say to the many British men who abandon their children, or never stop to wonder if they have fathered one?

He is slow to judge and suspects many of them have wives and children at home.

“The last thing they want is to have to disrupt their family by admitting to this kind of thing,” David says.



“It’s fear of the entanglement, fear of the commitment, of the financial consequences, fear of just the responsibility of having a child.”

And why do so many British men seek sex with Filipinos?

THE LAW By Margaret Simons Supporting your children is not only a moral responsibility, but also a legal one in almost all countries of the world, including the Philippines and the United Kingdom.

Coming to a sensible and amicable agreement between mothers and fathers is usually in everyone’s best interests.

But as a last resort, we find lawyers to act for the children and their mothers and go to court.

The United Kingdom and the Philippines have a reciprocal enforcement maintenance order arrangement. This means the British authorities and courts will enforce a

legitimate child support application from a Philippines-based parent.

The legal obligation to support your children does not depend on whether the mother and father were married, or had a long-term relationship.

If the father is not acknowledged on the birth certificate, then its more complicated and a special application with additional evidence, such as a DNA test, will have to be made.

If the father won’t provide DNA evidence, then an application can be made to the courts to make a declaration of parentage on the basis of any other evidence provided, and taking into account the father’s refusal. The courts can also order a father to do a DNA test if they decide it is in the child’s best interests.

If the British authorities decide a father is due to pay child support, then they use a formula based on the income of both parents to decide the amount. Failure to pay child support can lead to money being deducted direct from wages or pensions, or bailiffs can be sent to collect on the debt.

If a child was born on or after 1 July 2006 to a Filipino mother and a British citizen, then they are automatically British citizens. They can apply to the British Government for a letter to confirm this, and then for a British passport – but would have to provide evidence of parentage. Again, the courts can be asked to order a DNA test.

He says: “In the Philippines, it’s very easy to find a girlfriend, to be honest. If you come for a month, it’s easy to find a girlfriend who will stay with you for a month, and then maybe see you when you come again the next year, and that’s the way it works.

“Sometimes it’s a permanent relationship. Sometimes, as one of my friends put it in a French phrase, it’s ‘wife du jour’ (meaning, wife of the day).”

And what would he say to other British men who father children in the Philippines?



“It’s very difficult,” he says. “It depends on your circumstances.”

It was easy for David, as a middle-aged man without a wife, to stand by his child. It is harder for others.

But, he acknowledges, most British men with children in the Philippines could send even “a little money each month, if they wanted to”.

“Too many of them don’t want to, and that is hardly right,” he adds.

Put simply, William makes him happy. William is in the process of changing his name from Gutierrez. He may soon apply for British citizenship too.



Meanwhile, before he left, Roy agreed that he would help his daughters make an application for British citizenship. Soon, they hope to see him again in Britain and to connect with their half-siblings.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And after years of anger, they don’t hesitate when asked if they love their father. Melanie says: “Yes, I love him. I am now complete.”

News.title: Brit teen, 18, rushed to hospital after horrific crash in China during 6,000-mile charity bike ride from UK to Thailand
News.content:
BIKE HORROR Brit teen, 18, rushed to hospital after horrific crash in China during 6,000-mile charity bike ride from UK to Thailand

A BRIT teenager has been rushed to hospital in China after suffering a horrific crash during a charity bike ride.

Dyfan Hughes, 18, was left with head, neck and leg injuries during the middle of a mammoth 6,000-mile cycling trip from Wrexham to Thailand.



He is reportedly in a stable condition in hospital.

Dyfan embarked on the expedition with pals Louis Dennis, 19, and James Thomas, also 19, to raise money for the British Heart Foundation.



The trio, from Llangollen in north Wales, are undertaking the challenge in memory of Tony Edge, the dad of their friend Harrison, who died from a heart attack in 2024.

In a Facebook post announcing Dylan’s crash, they wrote: “We didn’t expect to be making this post.



“Dyfan has been in an accident, but he’s stable and in one of the best places in the world for this kind of accident to get the best recovery out of him.

“We don’t know what this means for the trip right now but one thing is for sure, we will stick together and when we arrive in Chang Mai, Thailand it will be the 3 of us no matter how long it takes.

“We will give more updates in the next few days.”

The trio have already managed to raise nearly £50,000 for charity, with donors praising their determination.



They all quite their jobs – Dyfan left bar work, Louis a factory post, and James a McDonald’s role – to embark on the cross-continental adventure.

The friends spend up to eight hours a day on their bikes and camp or stay in cheap accommodation.

Their JustGiving page reads: “We will be sharing every pedal, every flat tyre, every breakdown, on social media, and using the platform we build to point people to BHF.

“Thank you for the support.”

News.title: Anti-tourism zealots mock Brits with cruel World Cup banner as 2,000 protesters flood streets of Majorca
News.content:
ANTI-tourism zealots have mocked British holidaymakers with a cruel World Cup jibe as around 2,000 protesters flooded the streets of a Majorcan town.

Following England’s World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina, campaigners once again paraded a banner declaring: “The Only Thing Coming Home Is You.”



The brutal swipe at the Three Lions was carried through the picture-postcard streets of Soller as furious locals raged against what they claim is the island’s crippling tourism boom.

The march kicked off at 10am today in the stunning town nestled in Majorca’s Serra de Tramuntana mountains.



Protesters carried a huge banner reading “Soller al limit” – Soller has reached its limit – as they blasted the impact of mass tourism.

One demonstrator held a poster declaring: “No more second homes while locals can’t afford one.”



Another carried a stark message mixing English and Catalan: “Welcome to Majorca. And where do we live?”

The same World Cup banner that appeared during a fiery anti-tourist march in Palma also made a provocative return.

That demonstration on the island capital ended in violent clashes between protesters and riot police, with dramatic footage showing baton-wielding officers confronting demonstrators.

Police reportedly fired rubber bullets as tensions boiled over, with seven people injured, two seriously, and ambulances rushing to the scene.



More than 25,000 people were said to have flooded Palma for the protest, with campaigners accusing mass tourism of destroying locals’ quality of life.

Demonstrators screamed slogans including “tourists go home”, “tourism = destruction”, “save Majorca” and “less tourism, more life.”

One chilling banner showed a gun alongside the words: “Forced to live in struggle.”



The latest protest was fronted by platform Menys Turisme Mes Vida – Less Tourism, More Life – and also involved Moviment Jove de Soller, or Soller Youth Movement.

Organisers insisted before today’s march that it was “not against tourists or visitors”, but against an “unsustainable economic model.”

Campaigners claim the island is being strangled by soaring property prices, holiday rentals, packed public transport and parking chaos.

They also blame real estate speculation and the explosion in holiday lets for making affordable homes increasingly difficult for locals to secure.

The protest even caused a dramatic disruption to Soller’s bustling Saturday market.



Businesses in the centre were ordered to remove terraces and stalls normally placed outside between 10am and 2pm.

The restrictions were imposed following instructions from central government representatives in the area to protect public safety along the protest route.

The crackdown came on what is traditionally the busiest day of the week, when the Saturday market draws huge numbers of locals and visitors.



In the lead-up to today’s demonstration, the front of an estate agent in the town was also graffitied.

The furious scenes come amid a third summer of large-scale anti-tourism protests across the island.

Previous demonstrations have seen holidaymakers sprayed with water pistols, while last year a breakaway group of anti-tourist protesters reportedly confronted holidaymakers drinking at a popular Palma bar.

Earlier this month, around 10,000 campaigners formed a human chain to block access to the Playa Es Trenc beauty spot.

Activists insist locals are being priced out of their own communities by soaring demand from holidaymakers, second-home owners and expats.



A spokesman for the campaigners said: “Majorca is on the edge, and once again, everything points to increases in the number of visitors. No real change will come without sustained social mobilisation.”

He added: “That is why we are back on the streets. To defend the right to housing, territory, public services, language, culture, working conditions, and the future of Majorca.”

Police are also probing Less Tourism, More Life over online advice encouraging people to block Airbnb key boxes and vandalise firms linked to the tourism industry.

Shocking footage from earlier this year showed the extraordinary tactics being used by anti-tourist campaigners in the Canary Islands.



Videos showed fake police tape being used to cordon off popular beauty spots, including beach access paths, in a bid to fool tourists into believing they were closed.

Other footage appeared to show holiday-home key boxes being sabotaged with extra-strong glue.

The boxes are typically fixed to the walls of rental properties and contain keys which can be accessed using a PIN code provided by the owner.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Another clip showed a path to a popular volcano being sealed off with red and white tape.



A fake “no entry” sign was also put up in an apparent bid to keep tourists away.

News.title: Our town has been terrorised by masked ‘Gingerbread Man’ robbing women & OAPs for a YEAR… bungling cops can’t catch him
News.content:
FOR over a year a violent, masked thug has been attacking and robbing women of their jewellery, claiming over 50 victims – yet cops are no closer to catching him.

According to some victims, police have dubbed him ‘The Gingerbread Man’ because of his ability to escape their clutches.



But terrorised locals are now fed up.

They have posted a picture of a man alleged to be the offender online and even named him, yet the thug’s reign of fear continues.



There is even talk of vigilante justice.

Late last month, Stacey, 20, was walking to her retail job in the Chelmsley Wood area of Solihull along the Black Path when she passed a man in a balaclava.

It was 8.40 in the morning on a path normally full of mums on the school run but with the holidays having begun, it was quieter than normal.

Her mum, Sarah, 56, said: “My daughter told me that she held his stare as he passed by, then saw a shadow behind her as he doubled back on himself and grabbed her by the hair.



“He ripped a bracelet off her wrist and told her to “keep f***ing walking.”

Stacey, who is now being treated for PTSD, ran screaming to the nearby Asda and rang her mother.

Now her mum just won’t let it go. She said: “I have not stopped posting about it and soon I found out just how many other victims were out there.

“My inbox was full of people messaging me to say it had happened to them or tell me who it was, it seemed like an open secret.

“My daughter rang the police right after it happened on Friday 24 July and they said they’d check CCTV and get back to her later.



“They didn’t even take a statement. That man would have been covered in her hair and evidence if they’d got on with it.”

Solihull, on the outskirts of Birmingham, has long been seen as a posh area with a Conservative council and MP.

But included in the borough is Chelmsley Wood and Smith’s Wood, big council estates built in the 1960s after the city cleared its slums.



And that’s where the ‘Gingerbread Man’ has been running amock.

Now the charity Crimestoppers have offered a £10,000 reward for information leading to the conviction of the masked robber on the electric bike.

West Midlands Police have since admitted there have been over 50 victims in the past year.

Retired hairdresser Andrea Williams, 76, lives close to where several of the attacks have happened.

A neighbour, a woman in her 80s, was attacked last month as she pushed her walking frame on a path by her home.



She said: “My neighbour heard the screaming. She was punched in the face and was in a terrible state. He’d pulled her gold jewellery off her.

“This is a frightening place. It’s not well-lit and there are lots of dark alleyways and you see kids hanging out in balaclavas.

“I have been here 15 years and never go out at night but I would always walk to Asda which is only five minutes away but not now.”



While many of his victims are elderly females, some are younger and some are male.

Hairdresser Denise Tomlinson, 59, said her husband was attacked from behind as he walked home from work in Chelmsley Wood last October.

She said: “He was whacked to the floor and his chain was ripped off his neck.

“It was a really violent attack and left him needing to go to hospital with a sprained jaw and fractured ribs.

“The police were told everything but we never heard another dickie bird. I think they are useless.



“This thug is just laughing and thinks he can do what he wants. People need to lynch mob him.”

Denise’s customer Lynda Burden, 66, said she is too frightened to take her dog out at night.

“Hearing what he did to the old lady really made me think. My friend heard her screaming.

“This has been going on for far too long now. The police just fob everyone off.”

Another victim of the robber was Sian, a 24-year-old mother-of-two.



She was walking home from her aunt’s house in Smith’s Wood last April.

“It was 10.30 and it was dark and this guy walked past me wearing a balaclava.

“I tried not to think too much about it but then a few minutes later he came out of an alleyway and barged me onto the ground.

“He demanded jewellery and I did not have anything. He made me show him my neck and my wrist, then he demanded cash but I didn’t have any of that either.

“I think I was quite lucky really. He booted me as I lay on the ground and rode off.”



The impact of the crimes is affecting everyone in the area.

Lee, 44, a father-of-five, said: “We’ve been told this has been going on for 18 months. I think it’s outrageous.

“My daughter is about to go to senior school and needs to walk along the river where some of these attacks have happened.

“I worry about her, I worry about my wife walking back from the supermarket with the shopping.”

Mick Ryan, 68, a part-time cleaner, said: “If I knew who it was I would shake him out and claim the reward.



“He doesn’t pick on anyone who could fight back. He is just a coward and I hope he gets caught.”

Chief Inspector Jonathan Kiteley from Solihull Police said: “We want to reassure the community that we are doing everything we can to get this individual in custody.

“We have increased our patrols in key locations which includes both high visibility and plain clothes and we are continuing to review CCTV.

“When you’re out and about, be sure to be aware of your surroundings. Plan your route and keep valuables out of sight.”

Alan Edwards, West Midlands Regional Manager at the charity Crimestoppers, said: “This is a deeply concerning pattern of attacks against people who may be seen as more vulnerable, often carried out with little warning and using significant violence.



“Someone will know who is responsible or have information about these incidents.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“If you do, please tell us anonymously and we’ll pass it on for you. Your information could make a real difference in helping to protect others from harm.”

The Sun has approached West Midlands Police for further comment.

News.title: Boozed-up thug grapples with BA cabin crew & passengers aboard packed plane on Heathrow runway before being arrested
News.content:
A BOOZED-up thug was arrested for allegedly trying to attack British Airways passengers on a packed plane.

The foul-mouthed drunkard ignored repeated desperate warnings to “stay seated” from a brave woman crew member.



She told the flyer he would be “restrained” if he didn’t comply – and intervened several times to push him back into his seat.

Footage showed the drama onboard Flight BA275, carrying up to 331 passengers, as it approached the runway at Heathrow airport for take-off to Las Vegas.



The sozzled traveller was seen grappling with crew and other passengers in the carrier’s premium Club World cabin, where tickets can cost up to £7,000.

Take-off had to be aborted seconds from the runway and the abusive man – wearing a blue t-shirt and grey tracksuit bottoms – was removed by cops.



A video filmed by a fellow passenger ends with footage of several UK police officers leading the man away from the Airbus A350 in handcuffs.

One person forwarded the footage to BA – telling the airline to give the courageous female steward a pay rise.



Another person said on Instagram: “Time for cable ties and gaffer tape.”

The aborted take-off led to Flight BA275 leaving two hours, 38 minutes late on Thursday evening.

The plane eventually touched down in the US after a 10 hour, 17 minutes journey at 10.10pm on Thursday.

A Met spokesperson told The Sun: “Officers at Heathrow Airport were called at around 17:30hrs on Thursday, 6 August following reports of a passenger being disruptive on an outbound plane.

“The plane returned to the terminal to allow officers to board the plane. A 31-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of being drunk onboard an aircraft and failing to obey the commands of the pilot.



“He remains in police custody while further enquiries are carried out.”

A spokesperson for British Airways told The Sun: “Disruptive or abusive behaviour is never tolerated on board and the safety of our customers and crew is our highest priority.

“When these incidents occur, the appropriate action will always be taken.”

News.title: Daniel Kinahan extradition op underway as Govt jet travelling to Dubai for handover of Ireland’s most wanted fugitive
News.content:
DANIEL Kinahan will land on Irish soil for the first time in over a decade tomorrow ahead of being charged before the Special Criminal Court.

The 49-year-old is being brought home on the Government jet, which is expected to land at Baldonnel Aerodrome, the military airbase to the southwest of Dublin, on Sunday afternoon.



The Dassault Falcon 6X departed at 10.31am this morning and is currently in transit to Dubai.

Kinahan, Ireland’s most wanted fugitive, will be handed over by authorities in the UAE to specialist gardai, including those attached to the National Bureau of Criminal Investigation’s Extradition Unit.



When Kinahan lands back home tomorrow, he will be brought down the steps of the flight and met by a senior investigating officer who will formally arrest him.

It will mark Kinahan’s first time back in Ireland since February 15, 2016 for David Byrne’s funeral, who was shot dead at the Regency Hotel 10 days beforehand.

The major security operation on the ground will also kick in, with overtime in place for armed gardai in Dublin.

Kinahan will be transported to the Criminal Courts of Justice, and a short hearing at the Special Criminal Court will follow.



Armed officers will also be on patrol around the court, and members of the ERU and GNDOCB will also be inside the court.

Kinahan will be charged with directing the activities of an organised crime gang between 2015 and 2017.

The Irish Sun understands it is an all-encompassing charge that covers a range of crimes, including orchestrating a series of murders and attempts on life.

It is understood investigators will allege he is the man behind encrypted Pretty Good Privacy messages sent by ‘Cap’ and ‘Bon’.

This reportedly includes being in direct contact with Sean McGovern, named in court as the Kinahan cartel’s main man on the ground in Ireland as far back as October 2015.



Messages between ‘Cap’ and McGovern discuss Hutch associate James ‘Mago’ Gately just one month after the cartel murder of Gary Hutch in Spain.

Investigators suspect the gang was attempting to target Gately as far back as then.

Gardai will also allege Kinahan was in direct communication with McGovern in a botched attempt to kill Gerry ‘The Monk’ Hutch in Lanzarote in December 2015.

However, the majority of crimes Kinahan will be accused of being involved in occurred after the failed attempt on his life by the Hutch gang at the Regency Hotel, in north Dublin, in February 2016.

Cartel associate Byrne was murdered after he was shot six times when the Hutch mob stormed a boxing weigh-in at the hotel.



The Regency attack kicked off a bloody retaliation by the Kinahan organised crime group, with 18 lives claimed as part of the feud.

Detectives look set to contend that Kinahan can be linked to the alleged organisation of a series of murders and attempts on life over the following 14 months.

It will be claimed he was in constant communication with McGovern during this period.

Messages are understood to span up until Kinahan allegedly made direct contact with Imre Arakas, an Estonian hitman who was arrested before he got the chance to kill Gately in April 2017.

It is alleged Kinahan directed crimes mostly from Dubai, where he was arrested on April 17.



UAE cops swooped after officials examined a 200-page dossier detailing his alleged crimes after Ireland sought his extradition.

Since then, Kinahan has been in custody at Dubai’s notorious Al-Awir Central Prison.

The Dubliner launched an appeal against his extradition and was present in court on June 17, when he was told this had failed.

He then brought the matter before the UAE equivalent of our Supreme Court, which ruled against him. The decision came earlier than first thought, expediting security plans for his return, which was originally expected in September.

As part of plans for his return, a bomb and ballistic-proof van has been added to the prison fleet to transport Kinahan in a bid to thwart any escape attempt.



The armoured vehicle was bought from Northern Ireland and has recently been registered here as the State prepares for his return.

Sources say it has been modified to resemble other prison vans so Kinahan’s associates cannot easily identify it. After his appearance at the Special Criminal Court, he will be transported to Portlaoise Prison.

The secure van holding him will drive in convoy with armed gardai all the way to the Laois slammer.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kinahan will be housed in the A Block, its most secure block.

It already houses pal McGovern, who was caged for 24 years in June for his involvement in a murder and attempts to kill another target.

News.title: Britain set for glorious 36C highs next week as UK set for 5th heatwave – smashing 30-year record for sunny days
News.content:
BRITAIN is set for glorious 36C highs next week as the UK gears up for its fifth heatwave of the year.

The Met Office says temperatures will rise through the weekend as the hot spell builds across England and Wales, with yellow heat health alerts in force.



Forecasters add that temperatures could reach 30C on Saturday before climbing into the low 30s across southern and south-east England on Sunday.

The latest spell will be the fifth heatwave – an extended period of unusually hot weather for the time of year – to hit the country this year.



The hottest weather is expected on Thursday, when parts of East Anglia and the South East could hit a scorching 36C.

The Met Office says temperatures could reach around 30C across parts of England and Wales on Tuesday.



That could rise to between 32C and 34C on Wednesday before temperatures peak on Thursday.

And the sizzling spell could smash a 30-year record for the number of days Britain has reached 30C – temperatures have already reached 30C somewhere in the UK on 33 days this year.



The record stands at 34 days, set in 1995, and forecasters expect it to be broken next week.

Deputy chief forecaster Mike Silverstone said: “Temperatures will climb through the weekend and, more significantly, through much of next week.

“After a brief dip on Monday, high pressure will move across the UK before settling to the east, allowing a southerly flow to develop.

“A fairly widespread heatwave is likely across large parts of England and Wales, with hot conditions developing in places.

“The heat is expected to peak for much of England, Wales, Northern Ireland and Scotland on Wednesday, with up to 34C possible in parts of central and southern England and south-east Wales.



“East Anglia and south-east England, however, could see temperatures even higher on Thursday.

“Humidity levels are also expected to increase through the week, which may make conditions feel more uncomfortable, particularly overnight.”

Yellow heat health alerts have been issued for most of England until Tuesday.



They warn of possible impacts on health and social care services, as well as an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

The alerts are likely to be updated by the UK Health Security Agency in the coming days as the heatwave develops.

Temperatures will continue to rise as the weekend progresses, with the warmest weather expected in the south.

The UK has already seen some exceptionally hot weather this summer.

The year’s highest temperature so far was 38C, recorded at Lingwood in Norfolk on June 28.



The Met Office says there will be a clear split in the weather this weekend.

Scotland and Northern Ireland are likely to see some heavy rain, while England and Wales should stay largely dry and sunny.

But the long run of hot and dry weather has also left parts of Britain badly short of rain.

July was the driest month for England and Wales since records began in 1836, according to provisional Met Office figures.

Nineteen counties across England recorded just 1mm of rain or less throughout the whole of July.



Reservoir levels have also fallen, with storage in England now at 69 per cent.

That is down from 72 per cent a week earlier and almost 12 percentage points below the average for this time of year.

Five reservoirs have been classed as having exceptionally low levels.

They include Blagdon in Somerset, Hanningfield in Essex and Wimbleball in Somerset.

The dry weather has also increased the risk of wildfires, with conditions expected to be particularly severe across much of eastern and south-eastern England on Sunday.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Several major fires have already broken out across the UK in recent weeks, including blazes at Dunwich Heath in Suffolk and Headon Warren on the Isle of Wight.

The National Trust is urging people to sign a petition calling on the Government to make tackling climate change a national mission.

News.title: Widdecombe police reopen investigation into incident at Farage's home, BBC understands
News.content:
Counter-terrorism police investigating the killing of Ann Widdecombe have reopened an inquiry into an incident at Nigel Farage's south London home, the BBC understands.

It is understood to relate to what the Reform UK leader described as a "lit incendiary device" being pushed through his letterbox in April 2025.

Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) London said it was looking into an "attempted burglary" at a property as part of the Widdecombe murder investigation, but did not confirm the home was linked to Farage or why it might be connected to the killing of the former MP.

CTP London has also referred itself to the police watchdog over how the initial investigation into the Farage incident was handled.

Police said at the time that "damage was caused to a door but nothing was stolen".

Both CTP London and the Metropolitan Police were involved in enquiries. No arrests were made and the investigation was closed.

But on Friday, CTP London said a new line of inquiry had been identified that was not "pursued by them at the time".

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it had "decided to independently investigate the conduct of a Counter Terrorism Policing London staff member following a referral received earlier [on Friday]".

A statement continued: "The conduct relates to an allegation the individual failed to identify and pursue a line of enquiry relating to an attempted burglary reported in April 2025."

CTP London said it would "full engage" with the watchdog's investigation, adding: "The victims and families in both investigations have been updated today, and we continue to support them."

Ann Widdecombe, the 78-year-old former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman, was found dead at her home in Devon last month with serious injuries.

Joshua Kerry, from Rotherham in South Yorkshire, was later charged with her murder.

Kerry was initially arrested on suspicion of murder on 11 July, before being additionally arrested on 13 July on suspicion of the commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism.

Widdecombe had served as Tory MP for Maidstone in Kent for 23 years and was appointed to ministerial roles in Sir John Major's government in the 1990s.

News.title: Victims urged to come forward as police accused of 'litany of failures' over murderer and rapist
News.content:
Police have urged more victims of Simon Levy to come forward, as London's victims' commissioner said a "litany of failures" had allowed him to kill two women and rape a third.

Andrea Simons said a review into the "failure to monitor him appropriately" was needed after it emerged the 40-year-old was able to target his victims despite being known to police as a sexual predator.

British Transport Police (BTP) said women who recognised Levy as their attacker should report it, while the Metropolitan Police said it had actively investigated whether he had more victims, including further murders.

Meanwhile, the police watchdog confirmed two officers are being investigated over their handling of Levy.

The Independent Office of Police Conduct (IOPC) said a police constable was under investigation for gross misconduct, and a detective sergeant was facing a misconduct investigation.

The Met, BTP and Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) have all admitted failures in how Levy was monitored between his first conviction in September 2021 on sexual assault charges and his arrest for murder in September 2025.

On Saturday, Simons told BBC Breakfast a "multi-agency review" was needed, saying: "There was a lack of restrictions that could have been placed on him and a failure to monitor him appropriately - so all of those things, I think, we need answers to now."

Simons said public services "have to get better at recognising patterns of offending" before attackers become "emboldened".

The Met said its detectives had "exhausted numerous lines of enquiry - including working with coroners â to identify whether Levy is responsible for any similar, unsolved incidents, including deaths".

No further victims have been identified so far but the force urged "anyone who believes they may be a victim of his to contact police".

Levy is known to have attacked at least 10 women on public transport in London, seeking out busy carriages to assault passengers.

BTP said more women "may recognise [Levy] and have not yet reported what has happened to them".

News.title: Infantino denies claims Uefa paid off alleged 'lover' when he was general secretary
News.content:
Gianni Infantino's alleged lover was given a severance payment over the affair by Uefa while he was its general secretary, according to a Daily Telegraph investigation, external.

A spokesman for the now Fifa president was reported to have told the paper Infantino "strongly denies these categorically untrue allegations".

Uefa, for whom Infantino was general secretary from 2009 to 2016, issued a statement confirming "a departure payment was made to the individual in question".

The allegations come as Infantino fights for his future as Fifa president following his aborted plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

BBC Sport has contacted Fifa and Infantino for comment.

The Telegraph reported that Uefa paid a six-figure sum to the woman, who had an alleged relationship with Infantino, who is married, during his time at European football's governing body.

"Fifa president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue. Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory," a Fifa spokesman told the Telegraph.

"No employee at Uefa and Fifa has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino's behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved."

Uefa confirmed a payment was made to the woman in question and that it covered the fees for her to complete an MBA course at a local business school.

It said all payments were in line with regulations at the time, but those regulations have since been tightened and "reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation".

News.title: Hunter Biden tells BBC his pardon was 'not good' for US or his father's legacy
News.content:
Hunter Biden has told the BBC he was "the most privileged person there is" after receiving a presidential pardon from his father, former US President Joe Biden, acknowledging that it was not a good choice for America or his father's legacy.

In a wide-ranging interview with BBC Newsnight, Hunter Biden defended the controversial pardon, revealed his father's "painful" cancer has spread, ruled out seeking elected office and spoke about helping others recover from addiction.

Asked about the 2024 pardon, he said he understood the criticism but noted: "What would you have thought of my dad if he did not do that for me."

"It's something that is easily criticised and for good reason," he added.

"It's not fairâ¦ All I know is that I'm grateful that he did it for me," he said, acknowledging the pardon was "not good" for the American people, the constitution - or his father's legacy.

He argued to the BBC that his father ultimately acted out of concern that he would become a target under Donald Trump's incoming administration.

"I was the only one in the world that could have gotten what I got from the only person in the world who could give it, my father."

Hunter Biden also insisted he and his father had never discussed the possibility of a pardon before it was granted.

"There is no way that you can have those kinds of discussions that would not become public," he said.

President Biden granted his son a full and unconditional pardon in December 2024, despite repeatedly saying beforehand that he would not use the powers of the presidency to intervene in his son's legal cases. In announcing the decision, the former president said his son had been "selectively and unfairly prosecuted".

The pardon covered his son's federal gun conviction, a tax case he'd pleaded guilty to and any federal offences committed between 2014 and 2024.

News.title: Fifth heatwave of the year likely next week as temperatures could hit 35C
News.content:
Temperatures on Saturday will begin to climb above average again, reaching the mid- to high 20s Celsius in most of England and Wales.

It will be cooler in Scotland and Northern Ireland at 17 to 21C with more cloud, a bit of rain and a blustery wind.

By Sunday and into next week temperatures will rise even further with many parts of the UK exceeding their heatwave threshold temperature of 25 to 28C, depending on location.

With this hotter weather expected to last well into the week, many locations will have the three consecutive days needed to declare the fifth widespread heatwave of the year.

It has already been a remarkable summer in the United Kingdom with multiple records broken.

July has been the sunniest month on record for the UK, as well as the driest July on record for England and Wales.

There have so far been 33 days this year when temperatures have exceeded 30C in the UK. Next week, it is likely the record of 34 days, set in 1995, will be broken.

For the first time ever, a temperature of 35C has also been recorded somewhere in the UK on the three consecutive months of May, June and July.

It is possible August will join that list by the end of next week as some forecast models suggest 35C in central and south-east England.

News.title: I went for a full body MOT and the results came as a shock
News.content:
Annabel Mason-Thompson went for a Neko Health scan in September last year, knowing she had a suspicious-looking mark on her back - but it wasn't flagged by the technology.

"I felt a bit let down if I'm honest," the 50-year-old says. "Their AI scanner failed to pick up any of my four cancerous lesions.

"It was only when I went into the doctor's room after the scan and I pointed out my red mark did they take a look at it."

Further examination confirmed the mark was suspicious, so Neko Health contacted Annabel to say she would need treatment and wrote a letter to her private dermatologist to say the "lesion requires evaluation with a view to possible excision".

Her dermatologist found three more cancerous marks which needed urgent treatment.

"Luckily," she says, "they were all slow-growing basal cell carcinomas. I had to have two cut out and two taken off via cryotherapy."

Neko Health says "member safety and clinical excellence are at the heart of everything" it does. The company said its clinical team did identify a "lesion of concern" and it was reviewed by two of its dermatologists before a referral was made for potential treatment.

"We know that no one system is foolproof," Nilsonne says, "which is why we have multiple lenses - it is crucial that the technology and human expertise work together."

His company's latest data shows that of the 4,362 scans carried out on clients who visited Neko Health's Stockholm headquarters last year, 1.2% discovered life-threatening conditions such as melanoma and leukaemia. A further 4% spotted significant health conditions that required further treatment, and 1.2% flagged conditions that could be reversed such as pre-diabetic blood sugar levels.

While the figures are not representative of the population and only account for those who can afford to pay for this kind of preventive healthcare, Nilsonne says this is an indicator of how medicine should look in the future.

But GPs disagree. Prof Victoria Tzortziou Brown, president of the Royal College of GPs (RCGP), says they haven't seen "convincing evidence" private broad screening tests "improve health outcomes".

She says the results from these private scans can also place an additional strain on the NHS as clients come back for further tests and potential treatment, even "where the findings prove to be clinically insignificant".

News.title: He's been frozen on Everest for 30 years, now 'Green Boots' may finally be coming home
News.content:
For 30 years, a dead body known as "Green Boots" has been lying in the snow, nestled under an overhanging rock, not far from Mount Everest's summit.

The lime mountaineering boots worn by an Indian climber who died in 1996 have been a grim trail marker for many climbers on their way up the world's highest peak ever since.

Now India is looking for a specialist high-altitude recovery team to undertake a complex and risky mission to retrieve what they say is Dorje Morup's body â arguably the most famous of the hundreds whose bodies have been left frozen on the mountain.

Warning: This story contains a picture of a dead body.

They hope they are on the cusp of returning his remains to friends and family who never gave up hope he'd come home.

"On some days, before I went to sleep, I would think that there'd be a knock on the door tonight and that when I opened, he would be there," Morup's wife told the BBC.

"When he comes home, I will ask him: 'Where were you all these years?'"

News.title: Digital cameras and wired earphones are back and 'a bit more real'
News.content:
Luckily I'm out with my photography-loving best friend, who helps adjust the settings on the camera and gets snapping while I'm otherwise engaged on the dancefloor.

The mere sight of us pulling out the camera and squinting through its tiny viewfinder draws attention â "I've not seen one of these in years", a man remarks.

He's right â digital cameras had their heyday in the late 1990s and early 2000s, just before smartphones took off.

There are currently 42 million active film camera users globally, more than a third of these aged 18â30 and largely influenced by social media trends, according to a market research report, external last year.

So why, when we're surrounded by more advanced tech here in 2026, are they seemingly making a resurgence?

For Lily Redman, a 26-year-old content creator from South Wales, digital cameras "capture a quality that my phone just can't replicate".

She's been taking one on nights out and to concerts and feels the flash on her phone "is grainy and too high definition" compared to the "more smooth" finished product on a digital camera.

"I think people are looking for a bit of grit or something that feels a bit more real," she says.

That may also explain why low exposure photos taken on iPhones and Androids â where people dodge ready-made filters to artificially crank down the exposure setting and produce a darker image â are also popular on socials right now.

With digital cameras offering an element of surprise when you plug in the memory card reader to your computer at home, digital cameras capture a moment in time.

"If I look back at photos my mum took when I was two, they look so old but when I look at photos I took five years ago, they look like they were taken yesterday," says Redman.

"Phone photos have warped our perception of time."

News.title: Woman attacked by bed bugs during Travelodge stay
News.content:
Thirteen days after Hannah Stephenson stayed a night in a Travelodge hotel, she is still itching with red lumps over her body - a nightmare she would not wish on her "worst enemy".

The 31-year-old from Bassingbourn had been out with friends in Cambridge and decided to book a one-night stay at the hotel on Newmarket Road on 26 July to save money instead of getting a taxi home.

The next morning, she woke up to a "horrible realisation", feeling itchy with red lumps over her body and blood spots smeared on the bedding â the tell-tale signs of bed bugs, she said.

A Travelodge spokesperson said: "We are deeply sorry for Ms Stephenson's experience and how distressing an incident like this can be."

Stephenson said a lovely evening with friends had turned into a horrible morning.

"It was just a lovely wholesome time of Cambridge sightseeing and pubs, and now it is tarnished by these bedbug bites," she said.

"It wasn't until I saw the blood and the bugs that I realised what had happened."

News.title: Bristol Airport disruption a 'shambles' as flights restart
News.content:
Widespread disruption continues at Bristol Airport after a runway defect saw all flights suspended.

Hundreds of passengers were stranded after the airport's runway was closed from 18:00 BST on Friday until 08:00 on Saturday. While the runway has since reopened, the airport's website says the majority of flights are delayed or cancelled.

A spokesperson for the airport apologised for any inconvenience caused and advised passengers to check the status of their flight with their airline.

Dave Blackwell, travelling home from the Greek island of Rhodes, said it had been "a shambles" since his flight back to Bristol was diverted to Newcastle.

"We were in Rhodes Airport for three hours with no information. Now we have all been told our flight is going to Newcastle and then a five or six-hour bus ride - why Newcastle? How appalling," he said.

News.title: Strictly dancers Ola and James Jordan separate after 23 years of marriage
News.content:
Former Strictly Come Dancing stars James and Ola Jordan have confirmed they have separated after more than 20 years of marriage.

The former professional dancers were regulars on the show for several series after first featuring in 2006.

The couple's manager Vickie White confirmed the split, which was first reported by the Sun newspaper, external.

She said in a statement: "It is with great sadness that I can confirm that James and Ola began a trial separation some time ago.

"Their shared priority remains co-parenting their daughter, Ella, and they are committed to putting her wellbeing first.

"They would greatly appreciate your understanding as they navigate this difficult time."

Ola Jordan won the Open Polish Championship in 1999 when she was 17 years old and became James' dance partner shortly afterwards in March 2000.

She moved to England a month later and the pair got married in October 2003.

James appeared on Strictly from 2006 to 2013 while Ola appeared on the show until 2015.

Ola's celebrity partners included wildlife presenter Steve Backshall and Welsh sprinter Iwan Thomas, while James danced with former international gymnast and broadcaster Gabby Logan, as well as The One Show presenter Alex Jones.

News.title: Man guilty of fatal shooting of teen outside club
News.content:
A man has been found guilty of fatally shooting an 18-year-old outside a Wembley nightclub.

Tyrece Balcha was found with gunshot wounds outside the Crystal Club in Atlantic Crescent at about 05:30 GMT on 21 September 2025. He was taken to hospital, where he died four days later.

A jury at the Old Bailey found Ashley Wallace, 40, of Shenley Road, Southwark, guilty of murder and possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life.

At the same trial, two men were found not guilty of murder. A woman was cleared of possession of a firearm, possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life, and perverting the course of justice. The jury did not reach a verdict on a fourth man.

CCTV footage showed that Balcha had been involved in an altercation inside the club before being followed outside and shot.

Wallace fled the scene in a vehicle and was arrested on 25 September after police traced the car to south-east London.

A revolver carrying Wallace's DNA was found inside the vehicle, and investigators established that the bullet recovered from the murder scene had been fired from the gun.

News.title: Siân Phillips to step back from acting aged 93 after memory issues
News.content:
One of Wales' most celebrated actresses, Dame SiÃ¢n Phillips, is stepping back from full-scale stage acting after experiencing memory issues during rehearsals.

The 93-year-old made the decision after struggling to remember her lines while preparing for a recent production, according to The Times.

However, Phillips said she would continue performing in smaller projects, including a production with Michael Sheen's Welsh National Theatre next year.

Her career has spanned more than 80 years across stage, television and film.

Phillips told The Times she decided to stop taking on major stage productions after struggling to remember her lines during rehearsals for Atonement at Chichester Festival Theatre earlier this year.

According to the newspaper, she said she would continue performing in her show It's All Greek and is also due to appear in Samuel Beckett's Rockaby for Michael Sheen's Welsh National Theatre next year.

Born in Betws, near Ammanford, Carmarthenshire, in 1933, Phillips grew up speaking Welsh before learning English by listening to the radio.

She began performing as a child, appearing on Welsh-language radio from the age of 11, before studying at the University of Wales and later winning a scholarship to the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art.

She performed in radio productions such as The Archers and an adaptation of John le Carre's Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy, opposite Sir Alec Guinness.

Before her acting career took off, she worked for BBC Wales as a bilingual announcer and newsreader.

Phillips went on to become one of Britain's most acclaimed actresses, appearing in productions including Doctor Who, Calendar Girls, Dune, and I, Claudius.

She won a Bafta for her portrayal of Livia in the BBC's I, Claudius and received a Tony Award nomination for playing the title role in Marlene.

She was appointed a Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) in 2000 for services to drama, and then a Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire (DBE) in 2016.

News.title: Passengers 'stranded' at locked train station
News.content:
Translink has apologised after rail passengers were left stranded on a platform when a late-night train arrived into a station that was already shut for the night.

A group of about 30 customers were stuck on the platform at Newry Train Station for more than 45 minutes in the early hours of Saturday.

One of the passengers, Anne Greer, told BBC News NI it raised safety questions for the public transport company as the customers had no safe way to exit the station.

Translink said the firm was "looking into the incident" but added its train crew "remained with the passengers to ensure their safety while the issue was resolved".

The train was among a number of extra late-night services which are running to and from Belfast during the Fleadh Cheoil na hÃireann (Music Festival of Ireland).

It was scheduled to leave Belfast at 23:59 BST on Friday and it arrived in Newry at about 01:20 BST on Saturday.

"To our surprise the entire station was closed, so we couldn't exit," Greer said.

"So we're all trapped on the platforms for over 40 minutes."

She said the train crew "helped as much as they could, but there was nothing they could do".

"They were completely gobsmacked as to why they've arrived into a completely closed and locked train station."

Greer said she and other passengers tried to contact Translink but they could only find phone numbers for call centres which had also already closed for the day.

News.title: How asylum protests brought disorder to Thetford
News.content:
It is normally a quiet residential street but on Wednesday night, Clover Way erupted.

Residents later described their shock at seeing hundreds of people converging on an address where they believed asylum seekers were being housed.

It was one of five locations across the Norfolk town of Thetford that saw sporadic violence and disorder over three consecutive evenings, beginning on Tuesday.

Two police officers were taken to hospital, including one who had been bitten, and there were arrests on suspicion of offences including public order, harassment and possession of an offensive weapon.

Andy Symonds, the chair of the Norfolk Police Federation, said Friday night had been "much calmer", although "a number of people" had been dispersed using powers from Section 35 of the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014.

"We are on watch for tonight, it's the weekend. We will be dispersing people from the area," he told the BBC.

News.title: Man charged after four killed in lamp-post crash
News.content:
A man has been charged in connection with a crash that killed four people.

James Diggle, 27, of Alundale Road in West Derby, Liverpool, faces four counts of aiding and abetting causing death by dangerous driving.

The charge follows the deaths of four men, Jack Diggle, 23, Benjamin Dooley, 23, Andrew Roberts, 24, and Craig Shackleton-Brady, 26, who were killed when the black Cupra they were travelling in hit a lamp-post in Huyton, on Merseyside, on 24 July.

Merseyside Police said Diggle would be appearing at Liverpool Magistrates' Court later.

News.title: Man United v PSG LIVE: Michael Carrick’s men take on European champions in friendly in Sweden
News.content:
Man United continue their pre-season campaign against PSG ( Getty )

Manchester United face their highest-profile pre-season friendly of the summer as the tour of Scandinavia continues with a clash against double reigning Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain.

The Swedish city of Gothenburg plays host to the heavyweight clash, as Michael Carrick’s side look to build on a friendly campaign that has seen them win their previous two matches – including a 2-1 comeback win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm last time out.

PSG are an intimidating foe, although their star-studded squad will likely still be missing a number of players who played for France during their run to the semi-finals at the World Cup last month and they lost their previous friendly 3-0 to Mallorca. However, they will still provide a fascinating test as Carrick gears up for his first full season at the helm.

Follow all the action with our live blog below:

News.title: Irish government jet flying to Dubai for Daniel Kinahan extradition
News.content:
For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

A plane is on its way to Dubai for the extradition of alleged gangland leader Daniel Kinahan.

The Irish Government jet has taken off from Dublin, heading to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) for the extradition.

It comes after several months of preparations following the April arrest in Dubai of the Dublin boxing promoter who is an alleged leader of the Kinahan organised crime group.

Kinahan, aged in his late 40s, was detained on foot of an arrest warrant issued by the Irish courts in relation to alleged serious organised crime offences.

The Irish Government jet took off from Casement aerodrome in Baldonnel on the outskirts of Dublin on Saturday morning.

It is expected to touch down in Ireland on Sunday evening.

Kinahan’s arrest was carried out in accordance with a bilateral agreement on extradition between Ireland and the UAE.

The High Court in Dublin previously named Kinahan, who has recently been living in the UAE, as a senior figure in an organised crime gang involved in international drug trafficking and firearms offences.

The Kinahan cartel was involved in a feud with the rival Hutch crime gang in Ireland, which began in 2015 and resulted in 18 deaths.

In 2016, an attempt was made on Daniel Kinahan’s life at a boxing weigh-in at the Regency Hotel in Dublin.

After that, Kinahan left Ireland, first to go to the Costa Del Sol and later settling in Dubai.

He was identified in the High Court in Dublin as a senior figure who “controlled and managed” the operations of the Kinahan organised crime group.

In 2022, US authorities issued a reward of up to five million dollars (£3.7m) for Kinahan’s arrest.

This is a breaking news story. More to follow...

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal identify Vinicius Jr alternatives and Liverpool agree Barcelona defender deal
News.content:
Why Arsenal Want Bruno Guimaraes So Badly

Arsenal have moved on from their chase of Vinicius Jr after he signed a contract extension with Real Madrid and the Gunners have now reignited their interest in Atletico Madrid’s Julian Alvarez while PSG’s Bradley Barcola is also on their list.

But Bruno Guimaraes has finally officially completed his £75m move from Newcastle United with the deal for the 28-year-old midfielder representing a key piece of business of Mikel Arteta ahead of Arsenal’s title defence.

Rodri looks set to leave Manchester City amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid. The World Cup winning captain is into the final year of his contract and favours a move to Barca – though an initial offer of £38m has been rejected.

Liverpool, meanwhile, also want to sign Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and have lined up his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye in what could be a double swoop for Andoni Iraola’s side. The European champions may be willing to let them go, especially following Maghnes Akliouche signing from Monaco, while the Reds also look to have secured much-needed defender help with ex-Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo set for a loan deal, with an option to buy, at Anfield.

Elsewhere, Manchester United have added to their ranks by bringing in a teenage midfielder and they are exploring their options at left-back with Lewis Hall reportedly now set on a move to Old Trafford, but Newcastle are determined to stop the exodus and insist he is not for sale.

Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals with our live blog below:

News.title: Harry Potter star Jessie Cave reveals she earned more from one year of OnlyFans than ‘entire acting career’
News.content:

Actor and comedian Jessie Cave says she has made more money from one year of sharing hairbrushing videos on OnlyFans than she has done throughout her “entire acting career”.

The performer, 39, who is best known for her role as Lavender Brown in the Harry Potter films, started to post videos showing herself brushing her long hair on the social media platform last year, after dealing with rejection in the entertainment industry and struggling financially.

OnlyFans is a subscription-based platform best known for its adult content, although it is also home to plenty of creators who share non-sexual content.

Cave was clear from the start that her account would not be “a sexual one” and would instead focus on “sensual” videos of her hair.

Speaking to The Times, Cave, who shares four children with comedian fiance Alfie Brown, said that she had reached “a point of complete desperation” after being rejected from an audition.

“I couldn’t go and, say, work in a supermarket because I can’t afford the childcare, and also I don’t want people shouting Harry Potter spells at me as I work at Tesco,” she told the paper.

“I could retrain but I can’t afford to do a degree. I had a breakdown and I thought, that’s it with acting, I give up. But also we have no money. It was a point of complete desperation.”

open image in gallery The actor turned to OnlyFans after struggling to land acting roles ( Getty )

She initially thought that she would be on OnlyFans “for a few months” to “make five grand” and buy herself some “time to work out what we’re going to do”, but instead the income she has made on the platform has “genuinely saved our lives”.

Her subscribers pay $6 each month for access to her content, and she also earns additional income from “paid-for messages”.

Within just one day, she told The Times, she managed to earn back the £15,000 cost of her accommodation at the Edinburgh Fringe the year before, and she has “earned more, easily, than my entire acting career within one year”.

The actor admitted that there is “a stigma” attached to the platform because of its association with adult content, and said that she initially “didn’t really understand the risk of people thinking I’m doing porn”.

open image in gallery Jessie Cave (second right), with fellow Harry Potter cast members ( PA Archive )

Last year, Cave claimed that she had been left off the lineup at a fan convention because of her account.

“I found out that I didn’t get booked for a Harry Potter convention recently, as I’m now doing OnlyFans,” she wrote in her Substack.

“They explained it was because it’s a ‘family show and OnlyFans is affiliated with porn,’” she added. “This was baffling to me as some actors who do conventions (most actors, actually) have done TV and films in which they’ve done sex scenes and nudity. I’m just playing with my hair!”

OnlyFans has become a popular side gig for celebrities. In 2024, singer Lily Allen used the platform to share photos of her feet to paid subscribers, while musician Kate Nash has also used her account to raise funds for her live tour.

It is lunchtime in the seaside town of Clacton-on-Sea, and things are heating up.

It’s partly the stifling August temperatures, which have beckoned delighted holidaymakers to the English coast on a sweltering Wednesday afternoon. But there is also a curious energy coming from the town centre just a few streets away, where a small flyer is advertising an “open air public meeting” for candidates standing in the town’s upcoming by-election.

It isn’t clear if the meeting is even today, but regardless, a lively collection of three would-be MPs have gathered to make their case to any willing passers-by.

Voters in Clacton will go to the polls on Thursday to cast their ballots in a by-election triggered by the resignation of the incumbent MP, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, in July. It is an election widely touted as Farage versus Count Binface, with pollsters predicting the satirical candidate could take as much as 20 per cent of the vote. But on the ground, the reality is far less binary.

open image in gallery There are 34 candidates standing for election in Clacton ( PA )

Despite the fact that none of the major political parties is fielding a candidate, there are a record 34 people running to take Farage’s place – eight more than the previous record set at the Haltemprice and Howden by-election in July 2008. Some, like Nick The Incredible Flying Brick from the Official Monster Raving Loony Party, are hard to take seriously, but others are running on serious slates.

Neither Farage nor Count Binface are present for this “Speakers’ Corner” meeting, but several candidates have shown up. One, independent candidate Joseph 77, is wearing a yellow hard hat that says “Builder” across the front and standing next to a sign declaring: “Believe! Joseph 77 CAN WIN! Uplift Clacton AS YOUR NEW MP”, adorned with the St George’s flag and union jack. Another, Gerry Smith, is eagerly handing out leaflets with a young assistant.

“I'm going to be honest with you. I'm standing because I saw Count Binface being interviewed on Newsnight and it made me very, very angry,” Ms Smith says when I ask about her platform.

open image in gallery Nigel Farage is the frontrunner in Clacton ( PA )

“It made me very angry that people have not been respected in this town.

“I believe that people make Clacton, and the people of Clacton should be respected, and there should be a lot more infrastructure put into this area.”

She isn’t alone in this sentiment. While the wider public has undoubtedly enjoyed the narrative of Farage versus bin, people in Clacton told me they felt they had been made the butt of a joke that does little to serve their community.

Amy Smith, 37, said Clacton and its surrounding areas have been “let down” by Farage, who she said has “lots of talk” but has done little to help areas such as Jaywick – part of the Clacton constituency that has been classed as the most deprived area of England for four years on the trot.

She said she wishes the major political parties had taken “more of an interest” in the by-election.

open image in gallery Amy Smith, 37, said she hasn’t seen a lot of Farage ( The Independent )

“Like anyone else, we deserve a chance,” she said. “We have that stigma we can’t get rid of, the whole area. Oh, it’s Essex, or oh, it’s Clacton, or it’s Jaywick and that. But like every other seaside town, we need facilities.

“I don’t want it to end up like a typical seaside town.”

It’s the middle of the school holidays in an exceptionally hot and dry summer, the kind of day towns like Clacton were built to make the most of. There are holidaymakers here – parents push buggies as children dart around their feet and partners push loved ones in wheelchairs.

open image in gallery Many voters in Clacton said immigration is an important issue for them ( PA )

But aside from the tinny noises emerging from the colourful arcades, there is a muted quiet down the main road leading to the town’s Victorian pier, stretching out into the North Sea.

Sat on a bench near the town’s promenade, Ashley Scott, from nearby Kirby Cross, says that while he usually votes, he doesn’t plan on casting a ballot next week.

“None of the candidates really resonated with me,” the 35-year-old says, adding he believes Farage is a “waste of space”.

When I ask if he had seen Farage in the area since he was elected in 2024, Scott says he had seen him “once” – last week.

“I saw him last week on the ferris wheel making some content,” he adds. “But then before the place got busy, he just got in his Range Rover.”

open image in gallery Ashley Scott said he usually votes but isn't sure he will next week ( The Independent )

A regular voter, Scott says he had been left feeling “lost” by none of the major parties standing. “Count Binface is a funny character, but he’s not really serious,” he explains. “I don’t really know where to go, to be honest.”

On the other side of the road is the local Wetherspoons, which is heaving. As I walk in, a couple sitting at a nearby table spot my microphone and ask if I am a reporter. They tell me they are also candidates standing in the by-election. I ask if they went to the “open air public meeting” down the road, and they look at me blankly. Clearly, not everyone got the message.

Many in Clacton are still backing Farage, who is widely projected to win. Stopping to talk outside one of the arcades lining the road to the beach, Larry Graham, 73, says the Reform UK leader has his vote “without any doubt”.

open image in gallery Larry Graham said Farage has his vote ( The Independent )

“He’s the only bloke that will get this country out of trouble,” he insists. “If you vote for anybody else, we’re doomed.”

He says he’d even be prepared for Farage to make a pact with his ally turned rival, Rupert Lowe of Restore Britain, describing them as “on the same lines”.

But even some of those who favour a hardline stance on immigration – Farage’s flagship policy – say they are unconvinced by his rhetoric. Denise Pinkcombe, 61, says she wants the government to prioritise citizens over immigrants, but isn’t sure Mr Farage will bring about the changes she wants to see in her community.

“I’m not sure about Farage. I’m not sure I can trust him,” she says. “I want someone who will do something for the borough. Homelessness is a big problem here.

“When Andy Burnham started as prime minister, and he said he wanted to stop homelessness, I thought that was good.”

One couple said they want tougher action on small boat migrants, but are unsure the Reform leader will be able to actually fulfil his promises.

But despite having 34 options, most residents I spoke to said they didn’t really feel they had a choice at all.

“I’ve lost all hope,” one man says. “I don’t think I’ll vote for anyone. They’re all the same.”
