One in five people in Clacton would rather vote for Count Binface than in the upcoming by-election than vote for Nigel Farage, polls reveal.

A survey by Survation for Mandate Research of voters in Clacton suggests Mr Farage would win 73 per cent of the vote , while his main rival Count Binface, could sweep up an estimated 20 per cent of the vote.

In an Ipsos poll asking the general public who they would vote for in a hyperthetical head-to-head, a third (33 per cent) of British adults said they would prefer Count Binface to win the race, while only 21 per cent back the Reform UK leader.

Meanwhile, the poll found 32 per cent wouldn’t want either of them to win and 13 per cent didn’t know who they would chose.

Mr Farage initiated the by-election, which will be held on 13 August, in protest against parliamentary scrutiny of his financial affairs and backers.

All the main Westminster parties are boycotting the by-election in Clacton, meaning Labour, the Conservatives, the Liberal Democrats, Green Party and Restore Britain will not be fielding candidates.

Many have dismissed the election as a “stunt” , Yvette Cooper called the move by Farage a “political tantrum” and others said it was a “distraction” from allegations made about Mr Farage’s financial affairs.

The decision to force a by-election came after questions about a £5m donation Mr Farage received from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne and gifts from a convicted criminal, George Cottrell.

However, without other mainstream parties, the by-election is filled with numerous independent candidates as well as the satirical candidate Count Binface and actor-turned-politician Laurence Fox - who could steal 2 per cent of the votes according to a poll by Survation for Mandate Research.

Tendring District Council has confirmed a total of 34 candidates - a record for any parliamentary contest.

Count Binface – a satirical character who has pledged to cap the price of croissants at £1, conscript people who play loud music on public transport and build at least one affordable home – has now emerged as his main competitor.

For Westminster gossip, intrigue and behind-the-scenes insight, 

The comedian, who is described as an “independent space warrior” and wears a bin on his head, has contested a number of elections, including contests against Boris Johnson and Rishi Sunak and most recently the by-election in Makerfield, where he received 95 votes.

Labour under Sir Keir Starmer had struggled since they won the 2024 general election to contend with rising support for Reform UK, trailing behind as the Nigel Farage-led party stormed to victory making sweeping gains at two consecutive local elections.

But since Andy Burnham became prime minister polling shows the two parties are now neck-and-neck.

Data from YouGov shows 22 per cent would vote for Labour, 19 per cent would vote Conservative, meanwhile 23 per cent would vote Reform UK and 13 per cent for Green.

South Korea's national football association has issued a public apology following explosive media allegations that it provided "sexual services" to foreign referees over a decade ago.

The claims surfaced after a report by South Korean broadcaster JTBC on Thursday.

The report alleged that the Korea Football Association (KFA) offered such services to international referees on multiple occasions in 2011 and 2012.

This period included qualifying matches for the 2014 World Cup and the 2012 London Olympics held in the country.

Responding to the allegations, the KFA said: "We deeply apologise for causing concern over various issues involving the association, which emerged from a parliamentary hearing and an unprecedented search and seizure, and from reports about events from more than a decade ago, that even many within the organisation were unaware of."

JTBC's report cited a 2016 sports ministry investigation, which reportedly found that the KFA had provided "inappropriate entertainment" to foreign referees seven times between March 2011 and March 2012.

open image in gallery The association was already under scrutiny over a separate issue, involving the appointment of former national team coach Hong Myung-bo ( Reuters )

This included trips to massage parlours where the fees covered the costs of sexual services.

The KFA has not yet responded to requests for further comment or details regarding the allegations.

"The association makes clear that inappropriate conduct of this kind, or the use of corporate cards for such purposes, is absolutely not currently taking place," the KFA said in its statement.

The allegations add to scrutiny of the association over a separate issue, involving the appointment of former national team coach Hong Myung-bo.

Seoul police raided the KFA's offices on Thursday as part of an investigation related to Hong's appointment, police said.

Hong returned as national team coach in 2024 after a previous spell in charge from 2013 to 2014. His appointment drew scrutiny after the KFA abandoned a months-long search involving foreign candidates and selected Hong following a brief meeting.

The controversy resurfaced after South Korea's disappointing World Cup campaign ended in a group-stage exit.

South Korea were eliminated early from the competition after failing to build on the strong start that saw them come from behind to beat Czech Republic, subsequently losing their next two Group A matches to South Africa and Mexico.

The result was met with brutal condemnation from the country’s president and Hong resigned from his post in national disgrace.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: The best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds
News.content:
From gracious old farmsteads and magnificent manor houses to an ancient coaching inn creaking with Tudor character, the top luxury hotels in the Cotswolds combine a wonderful sense of history with contemporary style and outstanding modern British cuisine. Whether near picturesque Broadway in the north of the region or close to Bath in the south, location is a key attribute to them all: some offer serene escapes in acres of their own rolling parkland; others sit amid superb gardens; and several take over classic honey-stone villages that look as if they have been beamed in from a halcyon era of the past.

They all excel in providing creature comforts, whether crackling fires by kick-back sofas, canopy beds with soft throws, or suites with terraces and hot tubs. Facilities are top-notch too, ranging from beautiful bars and quiet terraces to blissful spas with inviting pools and even an opportunity for equine adventures. News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

Sports.title: Why does new Arsenal signing Bruno Guimaraes wear the number 39 on the back of his shirt?
Sports.content:
BRUNO GUIMARAES has completed a £75million move to Arsenal this summer.

The Brazilian midfielder has been one of Newcastle‘s standout performers since his arrival from Lyon in 2022 – and he leaves as a legend on Tyneside.



Guimaraes played 195 times for the Magpies, helping them to Carabao Cup glory in 2025 – the club’s first trophy in 70 years.

Now, the 28-year-old is looking to win more titles at Arsenal as he looks to help the Gunners to back-to-back Premier League triumphs.



Fans will be excited to see Guimaraes in red and they will notice his unusual choice of shirt number.

Why does new Arsenal signing Bruno Guimaraes wear the number 39 shirt?

Guimaraes has worn the number 39 since his days on loan at Athletico Paranaense as a youngster.

The number represented his father’s taxi number when he was working as a driver in Brazil.

Speaking about the choice of number in February 2023, Guimaraes said: “The number tells a story more beautiful than words can say. 39.

“I know people think it’s a weird number for a footballer. But for me 39 is special — no, it’s more than that. It’s magical.



“The number 39 gave me everything in life. It got me to Newcastle. It fed me, clothed me, and paid for three-hour bus rides to pursue my dream.

“#039 was the dispatch number of my father’s taxi in Rio de Janeiro.”

The number 39 shirt was vacant after Harrison Dudziak was released from the club.

Speaking on the move to Arsenal, Guimaraes said: “I feel amazing. I’m glad for the opportunity.

“Since the first time I spoke to [Andrea] Berta and Mikel [Arteta], I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.



“I’m so excited to join you. I will give you my best, I promise. Like I said, I’m your warrior, I’ll never give up.

“Hopefully we can create many, many good memories together.”

Sports.title: Former Tottenham striker Will Lankshear is first to be punished by new rule during Middlesbrough’s win over Wrexham
Sports.content:
MIDDLESBROUGH new-boy Will Lankshear confessed he was clueless about the EFL’s new time-wasting rule – after becoming the first player to break it.

Lankshear, who joined from Tottenham this summer in a deal that could rise to £20million, netted the only goal of Boro’s 1-0 win over Wrexham in the Carabao Cup on Friday night.



But he then unwittingly fell foul of a recently-imposed regulation designed to crack down on players taking an age to come off when substituted.

The fresh law cites that if a player takes more than ten seconds to come off when his number comes up in an EFL competition, then his replacement will only be allowed to enter the field of play at the first stoppage after a minute has elapsed.



It is the same rule that applied in the World Cup, and it will be active in the Premier League this campaign too.

Lankshear, 21, was subbed off in the 81st minute of Friday’s game at the Riverside, 20 minutes on from his spectacular, overhead-kick winner.



But because he took too long to come off, thanking his applauding fans as he left the pitch, his replacement Fin Cartwright was forced to wait more than 60 seconds before being introduced.

It meant Boro had to play with ten men for a short period.

Lankshear’s boss Kim Hellberg appeared to be aware of the new rule as he urged his striker to speed up his exit.

But Lankshear was none the wiser.

He later admitted: “I didn’t know!

“I haven’t been in the referee meetings at the start of the year because I came from Tottenham.

“I now know to get off the pitch a lot quicker!”

Lankshear came through at Spurs but is one of many youngsters the North Londoners have sold this summer to boost their own recruitment drive.



Luka Vuskovic, Tynan Thompson, Alfie Devine and Alejo Veliz have also all been shown the door, raising close to £100m.

Centre-back Ashley Phillips, 21, is set to make the same move as Lankshear when he completes a deal worth £7m plus add-ons from Spurs to Boro.

The Championship season does not kick off until next weekend but the first round of the Carabao Cup is taking place over this weekend.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes reveals he joined Arsenal to ‘make history’ as he completes £75million transfer from Newcastle
Sports.content:
ARSENAL have signed Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75million.

The Gunners confirmed the Brazilian’s arrival on Saturday, almost exactly a month after he asked to leave St James’ Park.



Guimaraes, 28, signed a four-year deal with an option to extend until 2031 after completing his medical on Thursday.

Newcastle had been reluctant to sell their skipper but they caved in after Arsenal offered to pay the full fee up front.



The North Londoners are long-standing admirers of Guimaraes, and Mikel Arteta was desperate to capture him in this window.

Former Gunners sporting director Edu started tracking him as a youngster at Athletico Paranaense and the club continued to keep tabs on him at Lyon and Newcastle.

Guimaraes said after his arrival: “Well, I feel good, I feel amazing. I’m glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to [Arsenal sporting director Andrea] Berta and Mikel [Arteta], I was excited.

“I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I’m so excited to join them, not only the Brazilians, we have an amazing squad here. I’m so excited to meet the other players, to start training. I just want to give my best.

“I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I’m in the right place to do it. I’m so excited to start.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We have tough games to play this season, so the squad is going to be very, very important and I’m hopeful we can achieve our dreams.

“[Declan] Rice sent me a message: ‘Come here and please no more fights, now we’re friends’. I was happy he messaged me, but the midfield we have here, in my point of view, is one of the best in Europe.

“Everyone is an amazing player, I’m so excited to start chatting and play, and know the players very, very well, but we have an amazing midfield.

“The message for me is thank you for everything you have done. All the messages you gave me, I’m so excited to join you. I will give you my best, I promise.

“Like I said, I’m your warrior, I’ll never give up. Hopefully we can create many, many good memories together.”



Berta welcomed Guimaraes to the Emirates and explained Arsenal went full on for his signature due to his versatility in midfield.

The Italian executive added the Brazil international will help Arteta further develop the North Londoners’ “playing style”.

Berta said: “We are delighted to welcome Bruno Guimaraes to our club. Bruno is a player with a great mentality and great quality, who will bring strong leadership to our squad.

“With Bruno joining us, we are further strengthening the heart of our team. As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player.

“He combines quality with quantity, and has provided goals and assists for his team every year.



“Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies.”

This has been a painful transfer window for the Toon, who have lost a raft of key players and manager Eddie Howe.

Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali were both sold for big money, but the looming sale of Guimaraes was reportedly the “final straw” for Howe, who quit last week.

New boss Matthias Jaissle should have cash for a rebuild but about £7m of the Guimaraes fee will go to Lyon, who are entitled to 20 per cent of the Magpies’ profit.

Guimaraes broke down in tears as he said goodbye to his Newcastle team-mates.



He said in a statement to the Toon: “This is one of the toughest decisions of my life. When I arrived, the club was in a challenging position and I am incredibly proud of what we achieved together.

“I fell in love with this place. I really mean that. From my first day, the supporters, my teammates, Eddie and the staff, and everyone connected with the club made me and my family feel at home.

“I thank PIF, our chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan and Jamie Reuben for everything they have done for me and for this football club. I also want to say thank you to David and Ross for the huge respect to me throughout this process. They did everything they could to keep me at Newcastle, and I am very grateful for our time together.



“This move is very tough because Newcastle means so much to me, but I wanted to experience something new in my life. I feel ready for a new challenge for myself and my family. I had a very positive conversation with Matthias Jaissle, and I leave knowing the club is in very good hands.

“To the supporters, thank you will never be enough, but I say it with all my heart. I will always be proud to have been part of this club’s journey. Thank you for everything.”

Arsenal had already signed Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier this summer, as well as making Piero Hincapie’s loan move permanent.

But the signing of an established Premier League star in Guimaraes will take their squad to another level.

It will also relieve some of the burden from Declan Rice, who played over 60 matches for club and country last season and carried niggling injuries into the World Cup.



All-action Guimaraes, who scored nine league goals last term, can also bring an attacking flair to the midfield.

Josh Kroenke described Rice as a “plug-and-play” signing when Arsenal splashed £105m on him in 2023.

And his arrival will make up for missing out on Vinicius Jr, who opted to sign a contract extension at Real Madrid after being courted by the Gunners.

Sports.title: Phil Parkes dead at 79: Wolves Hall of Fame inductee who was part of Uefa Cup final team dies as tributes pour in
Sports.content:
WOLVES legend Phil Parkes sadly died this morning at the age of 79.

Parkes is one of the greatest goalkeepers to ever play for the club, who added him to their Hall of Fame after his amazing 18 years at Molineux.



Wolves issued the following announcement: “Legendary Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes sadly passed away this morning at the age of 79.

“A larger than life character and a true Wolves hero that will be missed by everyone associated with the club.”



Parkes joined the Wanderers in 1960 at the age of 13 and spent four years with the youth team.

The West Bromwich native was quickly affectionally nicknamed ‘Lofty’ due to his 6’4″ frame between the sticks.



Wolves added the following tribute: “The thoughts and prayers are with Lofty’s loved ones at this sad time. Details on further club tributes will follow.”

Parkes joined the first team in 1964 but made his legendary debut two years later in style as he saved a penalty in a 3-2 win over Preston North End.

The keeper went on to amass a whopping total of 382 appearances with the first team.

The Wolves legend quickly established himself as a key player during the Bill McGarry era and broke a club record for consecutive league games.



Parkes played 127 matches in a row during the early 1970s, a record which may never be broken.

Lofty was instrumental in Wolves’ journey to a first ever European final back in 1972.

Parkes saved two penalties in the Uefa Cup semi-final against Ferencvaros, before collecting a runner-up medal following a narrow 3-2 defeat to Tottenham in the final at Molineux.

Two years later he played in every round of Wolves’ journey to the League Cup final at Wembley but was denied an appearance in the showpiece event that saw his team winning 2-1 against Manchester City due to injury.

Parkes bowed out in 1978 with a victory in his final game against West Ham.



After retiring in 1983, he settled back in Wolverhampton serving on the committee of the Former Players’ Association and remaining a regular presence around Molineux.

But Parkes suffered a serious fall at home last year and that led to emergency surgery on his back.

That injury left him under medical supervision until his passing today.

Asked in 2024 how he’d like his Wolves career to be remembered, Parkes said: “I hope my Wolves career is remembered with joy.

“I loved playing for this football club, I had a great time, so I just hope all the supporters enjoyed it too.”



Wolves fans pay tribute

Upon hearing the news, Wolves fans immediately stormed social media to share their tributes for Parkes and his incredible career.

One supporter tweeted: “A true Wolves legend and wonderful man. Will be missed, Wolves and the fans will honour him on Friday I’m sure. Love and thoughts with his family RIP Lofty.”

Another commented: “Rest in peace Phil.”

A third wrote: “We have lost not only a legend but a true gentleman! Always had time for others ! Really sad news to wake up. RIP Lofty you legend.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

This fan said: So sorry to hear this. It was a pleasure to have had the chance to meet and chat with him. A club legend. Sending condolences to his family, friends and former team-mates. He will never be forgotten.”



And that one added: “Such sad news, had the pleasure of meeting Phil. Spoke about Wolves in great detail and such a lovely chap. Rest in peace.”

Sports.title: Former Premier League club’s 62,500-capacity stadium in bid to host fewer sporting events
Sports.content:
WEST HAM’S 62,500-capacity home could host fewer sporting events and more concerts under plans aimed at tackling the stadium’s £19million annual losses.

London Stadium LLP is seeking permission to increase the number of concert days it can stage from 10 to 24, while reducing the annual number of sporting events from 87 to 70.



The venue, which is owned by the Greater London Authority, says the changes would allow it to attract more major non-sporting events and improve its finances.

A spokesperson told the Local Democracy Reporting Service via BBC News: “There is no impact on West Ham matches or their capacity. West Ham are entitled to play matches at the stadium as per the concession agreement.”



West Ham declined to comment on the proposals.

The Hammers moved into the London Stadium in 2016 after leaving their famous Upton Park home, with the venue having originally been used for the 2012 London Olympic Games.



West Ham had spent every season back in the Premier League since moving there until their recent relegation, meaning their return to the Championship will now have a direct financial impact on the stadium.

Lyn Garner, chair of London Stadium LLP, said the venue had been losing around £19m every year for some time because of its long-term deal with West Ham.

She described the 2025/26 campaign as a “particularly bad year for London Stadium” after it hosted only two summer concerts.

West Ham’s relegation has made matters worse, with the club’s annual rent falling from £4.6m in the Premier League to less than half that figure in the Championship.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The stadium now wants to make itself more attractive to the music industry by increasing the number of concerts it can host.

It is also seeking to raise its concert noise limit, with the current rules allowing six events at 75 decibels and four at 65 decibels when measured from nearby buildings classed as sensitive receptors.

Under the proposed changes, every concert would be allowed a 75-decibel limit – a move the stadium says would help it compete with Wembley and Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, which has more lenient limits.

The timing comes as the Hammers prepare for life outside the Premier League, with Portsmouth visiting the London Stadium today in the first round of the EFL Cup.



It will be West Ham’s first match of the new campaign before they travel to Turf Moor next Sunday to face Burnley on the opening weekend of their Championship season.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho introduces three ‘strict’ new rules at Real Madrid as he stamps his authority on squad
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO has reportedly laid down the law with three strict rules to kick off his Real Madrid revamp.

The former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham boss returned for his second stint at the Bernabeu in June – 13 years after he left.



Mourinho will be tasked with getting the best out of Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior this season.

And he has wasted no time tightening up discipline in a group with some big personalities.



According to AS, his new deal-breakers are centred around food, punctuality and recovery.

First off, Real’s nutritionist has been given more authority to instruct the players on what to eat for every meal, every day.

The nutritionist used to take on more of an advisory role, but their recommendations are now compulsory.

And although that takes freedom away from the players, they are said to have reacted positively to the change.

From that alone it is clear that Mourinho means business – and his approach to lateness is just as firm.

Whereas Los Blancos’ super-rich stars used to be fined if they were late to training or team meetings, Mourinho will now make them train separately from the main group.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The boss, 63, has implemented this as a blanket rule for the entire squad, with solo gym workouts lined up for those who break it.

Mourinho has also put measures in place to stay on top of injuries.

From now on, under the Portuguese’s watchful eye, every recovery session will take place at Real’s Valdebebas training base.

The idea is to deal with all medical issues in-house so that club staff are across every detail.



Mourinho was a surprise appointment by Florentino Perez, with the veteran manager’s career appearing to tail off during stints in Turkey and Portugal.

But he will be out to prove there is still life in the old dog when Real get their competitive campaign underway at Espanyol on August 22.

I'm so excited to join you. I will give you my best, I promise. I'm your warrior, I'll never give up. Hopefully we can create many, many good memories together.

The Brazilian gives Arteta even more options and it also allows for the possibility for Rice to get a breather in certain games after his exploits last season.

It is a world-class midfield and if Arsenal were not favourites for the title already, they are now.

Question marks were being raised over the fee Newcastle wanted for a player who will be 29 in November but the deal has been done nowhere near the reported £100m fee that was wanted. At the start of the transfer window, you would have probably said this is a fair fee, but with the last few weeks we have had in the window, with big money spent on midfielders Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers, anything under £100m looks good value.

Guimaraes is a little older but this is Arsenal's strategy, they want to win now. They have signed some younger players but last summer's deal to sign Viktor Gyokeres was to win now. He will not need any time to settle in. He is one of the most consistent Premier League midfielders.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jay Bothroyd thinks Guimaraes is an upgrade for Arsenal's midfield and will play alongside or fill in for Declan Rice

Arsenal will not necessarily make money on him in the future but his arrival should get them closer to winning a first Champions League and he may help them retain the Premier League title.

If they can add a left winger and some star quality in that position, which looks like the last piece of the puzzle, it could be bad news for their title rivals.

'Newcastle were desperate to keep Guimaraes'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Keith Downie explains the three reasons why Newcastle have allowed Guimaraes to leave the club for Premier League champions Arsenal

Sky Sports News reporter Keith Downie:

Newcastle were desperate to keep Guimaraes and if he had said he wanted to stay, Newcastle would have refused any offer from Arsenal or any other club.

Attempts to persuade Guimaraes otherwise were made and positive conversations were held, but he was insistent he wanted to leave because he felt this was his last big opportunity to win titles.

The deal could only go ahead if two things happened: Guimaraes said he wanted to leave (which he has respectfully) and Newcastle sold on their terms, similar to Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.

Newcastle insisted it was their valuation or no deal. They would only sell Guimaraes at a fee that would become one of the highest paid for a player aged 28 or over.

In addition, a deal would only be sanctioned if the situation was handled properly - for example, Guimaraes attending Newcastle's training camp in Spain, which he reported to on Monday.

Newcastle feel Guimaraes has complied with their demands immaculately. They did not want a repeat of the Alexander Isak situation, where he refused to train before joining Liverpool last summer.

Agents were in between the clubs from the outset but Newcastle refused all pushes, which had began with mentions of a deal worth £40-£45m in June.

Newcastle were left frustrated because they felt Arsenal elongated the transfer by refusing to contact them for weeks.

Newcastle insist there have been no fall outs and good relations remain between player and club.

Sports.title: 'I'd rather fight Aaron for world title' - Walsh dismisses Stevie McKenna call-out
Sports.content:
Callum Walsh would entertain a fight against Aaron McKenna over Stephen McKenna, insisting all-Irish clashes only make sense with the world title on the line.

Walsh (16-0, 11 KOs) fights former European champion Tyler Denny on the undercard of Aaron McKenna's IBF world middleweight title showdown with Etinosa Oliha at Dublin's 3Arena this Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

It's the headline act of six middleweight bouts on a stacked card that also sees Stephen McKenna face Owen O'Neill over eight rounds before assuming corner duties for his younger, world title-chasing brother.

Walsh has been identified as a potential future opponent by Stephen McKenna (16-1, 15 KOs), but the unbeaten 25-year-old believes he's already at another level.

Responding to McKenna's challenge, Walsh told Sky Sports: "If there's anyone that I'm looking at, it would be the fella with the world title, not the fella with the loss.

"In my mind, it doesn't make sense unless it's for a world title. There are bigger names than Stevie McKenna calling me out.

"Shane Mosley Jr is a bigger fight than Stevie McKenna. His brother Aaron is fighting for the world title. If I was going to fight either of them, I'd fight Aaron for the world title."

Image: Walsh on the scales ahead of his middleweight fight against Denny (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa Boxing)

'It makes sense for him, not for me'

Walsh believes an all-Irish fight without a world title on the line could needlessly jeopardise the momentum middleweights are currently generating in Ireland.

"It's a big time for Irish boxing," he added. "As an Irish fighter from such a small place, there are three of us now in Zuffa Boxing. Why would we want to eliminate each other unless it's for a world title?

"If it's for a world title, at least you can get paid for it. You're going to be able to sell out an arena and put on a big show for everyone involved. Why have an all-Irish fight on an undercard somewhere when it doesn't make sense?

"It makes sense for him. It makes no sense at all for me. His brother's fighting for the world title. There are bigger names calling me out. I've had bigger fights. It doesn't make any sense."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stevie McKenna is determined to have an all-Ireland clash against Walsh should both of them emerge victorious at Zuffa Boxing 10 this weekend

Walsh believes Stephen McKenna would be better served avenging his sole loss as a professional, a majority-decision defeat to Lee Cutler in 2024.

"He doesn't even want to fight the fella who beat him," he said. "He was asked if he wanted a rematch and he said no.

"Go back and fight the fella who beat you. That's the one I'd be looking at if I was him. He's in the same division, the same league, and he's begging for the rematch."

'I'll fight Aaron or the other fella'

Walsh, who fights in Dublin for the first time since knocking out Przemyslaw Runowski in two rounds in 2024, is confident he can overcome Denny and believes Aaron McKenna will become Ireland's newest world champion.

Victory for both men would set up the mouth-watering prospect of an all-Irish world title fight, and Walsh insists he would have no problem facing Aaron should he emerge as champion.

"I don't know much about his opponent, to be honest," Walsh added. "I'm sure Aaron will win. I presume he will.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Walsh insists he's not complacent ahead of Saturday's fight with Denny, while the former European champion is confident he can cause the upset in Dublin

"It's a big opportunity and a big night for him to go out there, perform and win the world title in Dublin. I think he will.

"If Aaron wins and they want me to fight him, I'll fight him. If he doesn't win, maybe I'll fight the other fella.

"I just fight whoever they tell me to. I'm not out here calling anybody out. It's just the same old habits."

Watch Zuffa Boxing 10, headlined by Aaron McKenna vs Etinosa Oliha live on Sky Sports this Saturday.

Sports.title: Where does Guimaraes fit in at Arsenal?
Sports.content:
It is easy to understand why Arsenal have signed Bruno Guimaraes. The now ex-Newcastle captain is one of the Premier League's most complete midfielders, capable of dominating and destroying but also scoring and creating, with passing ability to match his physicality.

The Gunners have signed the 28-year-old for £75m, and he joins a group of midfielders already including Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi, Martin Odegaard, Mikel Merino and Myles Lewis-Skelly. So, where and how does he fit in?

No 6 or No 8?

Guimaraes can play as a deep-lying midfielder or a more advanced No 8. He explained his preference for the latter position in an interview with Sky Sports in October 2022, when he was being used by former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe in the No 6 role.

"To be honest, if you ask me this question, I have to say I prefer to play at No 8, but I think my role here, at No 6, is exactly what the team needs," said Guimaraes. "It is to take the ball out, to do some passes, to find the wingers and the strikers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Keith Downie explains the three reasons why Newcastle have allowed Bruno Guimaraes to leave the club for Premier League champions Arsenal.

"I can play both positions, but Eddie has a choice to make and, for me, the most important thing is just to play and to help Newcastle get the three points. I think my best position is at No 8 but I can play at No 6. It's not a problem for me."

Guimaraes ended up playing in his favoured role for Newcastle after Sandro Tonali took over at No 6, but his flexibility, and willingness to put the team first, will doubtless appeal to Mikel Arteta, who loves players able to slot into different positions.

Guimaraes' versatility shines through when breaking down his minutes played by position in the Premier League.

The graphic above shows he has played most of his minutes for Newcastle at the base of midfield but also highlights his ability to play as both a right and left-sided No 8, providing further evidence of the flexibility he can bring to Arsenal in terms of how he is used.

Arsenal have already hinted at their desire to make the most of Guimaraes' abilities in both roles, with sporting director Andrea Berta stating he was signed to help the squad "develop [its] playing style" while also adding competition to Arteta's midfield.

"As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity, and has provided goals and assists for his team every year," Berta said.

"Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies."

The options he gives Arteta

Guimaraes himself describes his style as that of a "warrior" - but one who can play too. "I'm good with the ball, composed, very calm," he added upon his signing.

Even when ostensibly starting as Newcastle's No 6, Guimaraes was platformed to attack. "With the way we are playing, Dan Burn is at left-back, so he can stay in the middle and I can go and be another player to help the attackers," the Brazilian added to Sky Sports in 2022.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Bruno Guimaraes' best goals for Newcastle as he is linked with Arsenal

Guimaraes finished that season with four goals and five assists in the Premier League for Newcastle, despite playing as the No 6. He was even more productive in the following campaign, scoring seven goals and providing eight assists in the same role.

In total, the midfielder contributed an impressive total of 30 goals and 25 assists in 153 Premier League appearances for the club, underlining the extent of his attacking threat.

Arsenal have plenty of full-backs capable of tucking inside to allow him to get forward from the No 6 position. But another way to maximise Guimaraes' attacking qualities in a box-to-box role would be to use him as part of a double pivot.

Rice could be the perfect foil.

The 27-year-old spent most of last season playing as Arsenal's left-sided No 8, with Zubimendi playing at No 6. But he finished it playing further back, on the right of a double pivot with Lewis-Skelly, who impressed after his late-season move into midfield.

Rice excelled alongside the youngster. Like Guimaraes, he has the energy to get up and down the pitch as a box-to-box midfielder but he is also tactically aware and disciplined in his positioning.

Image: Bruno Guimaraes joined Newcastle from Lyon for £40m in 2022

Even before he was moved back into a double pivot last season, Rice often provided cover for Zubimendi, who was able to score five Premier League goals while playing as Arsenal's No 6.

Using Guimaraes and Rice in a double pivot would allow Arteta to deploy one of Martin Odegaard or Eberechi Eze as a pure No 10. In the event of Rice being unavailable, or simply needing a rest, he could even use both players as No 8s, ahead of Guimaraes at No 6.

If Arteta wanted to go in the opposite direction and prioritise physicality over flair, he could sacrifice a playmaker for Zubimendi and push Guimaraes forward, into the right-sided No 8 role in which he spent much of the last two seasons for Newcastle.

A midfield trio of Guimaraes, Zubimendi and Rice might not appear the most attack-minded but it would certainly allow Arsenal to win most physical battles in central midfield. It should also be noted that Guimaraes actually profiles similarly to Odegaard as a passer.

He also directed a similar percentage of passes forward to Odegaard, and was in fact more efficient in terms of forward-pass accuracy.

The numbers reflect a capacity to unlock opposition defences which could mitigate Odegaard's absence, at least to some extent, while providing another source of creativity from central midfield.

Would others lose out?

The arrival of Guimaraes does inevitably raise questions about some of Arsenal's other midfield options but is easy to see the logic behind their efforts to land a player of his quality.
