World.title: Congress lost the millennials. Can it win over Gen Z?
World.content:
's interaction with Kalavati went viral in 2008, back when "viral" meant something very different. The widow of a farmer who died by suicide, she was raising nine children in Vidarbha when Rahul met her, and he later invoked her life in Parliament during the Indo-US nuclear deal debate.

Eighteen years later, the Leader of Opposition stood beside Rhiya Ahir, the 27-year-old Mumbai woman who became a social-media sensation during the student protests after standing in front of a police van carrying detained protesters.

Between those two moments, an entire generation grew up and largely walked away from the Grand Old Party in search of

achhe din

. Broadly speaking,

lost the millennials in large parts of the country, barring the South.

Now, as anti-incumbency gradually catches up with the ruling regime, Congress is looking at a fresh crop of voters who could form a decisive electoral bloc by 2029.

Rahul's communication strategy over the past month has laid out the approach clearly. From an unparliamentary expression inside Parliament that was later expunged, to telling protesting students they did not need to apologise to the prime minister, to an Instagram outreach mixing serious student questions with playful jibes at â

â, the attempt to speak Gen Z's language is unmistakable.





Former Congress leader

, speaking to TOI, said he believes Rahul's natural lingo is more attuned to Gen Z than Modi's. He says the prime minister's recent Instagram outreach came across as condescending to sections of young users, while Rahul seems more natural. Jha is categorical, according to him, Rahul represents the future and Modi the past.

Despite successive Assembly victories after its underwhelming 2024 Lok Sabha performance, the BJP suddenly appears to be on a slightly sticky wicket.

The NEET agitation has claimed a high-profile political scalp, a rarity in this government. For Rahul, it is a no-brainer to cash in on that advantage.

The generation that got away

The generation that was in its 20s and early 30s during the 2014 election firmly reposed its faith in the BJP or, more specifically, in Narendra Modi. His appeal as an outsider breaking through Delhi's entrenched power elite resonated with aspirational young voters.

The pitch around development, technology, entrepreneurship and muscular nationalism continued to reap dividends election after election.

An analysis of Lokniti-CSDS National Election Study data shows BJP support among voters aged 18-25 rising from 34% in 2014 to 41% in 2019. Congress remained stuck at 19%. The personal gap was even wider, with 51% of young respondents preferring Modi as prime minister in 2019, against 23% for Rahul.

The BJP did more than defeat Congress among the young; it captured their imagination about what the future could look like. By 2024, however, a subsequent Lokniti-CSDS analysis found that no party had succeeded in carving out a distinct youth constituency. That churn is precisely what makes 2029 interesting.

The beauty of democracy is that there is always a fresh test after five years. The next general election can be a very different proposition, or at least that is what Congress would hope.

The 36-crore election

By 2029, Gen Z will be far from a niche constituency.

Using the common definition of Gen Z as those born between 1997 and 2012, its voting-age members in 2029 will be roughly 18 to 32 years old. An interpolation of the National Commission on Population's 2026 and 2031 age-group projections suggests India could have around 36.4 crore people in the voting-age Gen Z cohort by then. These are projected people of voting age, not registered electors, and actual turnout will obviously be lower.

The arithmetic is still striking. Uttar Pradesh could have around 6.65 crore Gen Z adults in 2029, Bihar 3.73 crore, Maharashtra 3.18 crore, West Bengal 2.40 crore, Madhya Pradesh 2.34 crore and Rajasthan 2.25 crore. Gujarat could have 1.86 crore, Tamil Nadu 1.67 crore, Karnataka 1.63 crore, Andhra Pradesh 1.22 crore, Odisha 1.15 crore and Telangana around 92 lakh.

Supporters of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) celebrate after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned

Together, these 12 states could contain nearly 29 crore voting-age Gen Z Indians.

On the current electoral map, they account for 420 Lok Sabha seats, though delimitation could change that arithmetic before 2029.

Awkwardly for Congress, it remains organisationally weak in several states where the Gen Z pool will be largest. Uttar Pradesh and Bihar alone could contain more than 10 crore Gen Z adults. Instagram can reach these voters, but holding on to them requires organisation.

Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy has taken the outreach a step further, proposing that the minimum age to contest Lok Sabha and Assembly elections be lowered from 25 to 21, and that for the Rajya Sabha and legislative councils from 30 to 25.

But the question comes back at Congress. Even if the legal age is lowered, will it actually give tickets to 21-year-olds?

The break Congress could not manufacture

The party has been trying, with limited success, to get into the youth mind space for years. Rahul's campus visits, student conversations, attacks on unemployment and repeated interventions on paper leaks all predate the present protest cycle.

The Bharat Jodo Yatra tried to remake Rahul as a leader who would walk and listen rather than merely speak.

The Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra before the 2024 election sharpened that pitch. That eventually became the five-part Yuva Nyay offer. Yet it did not acquire a life beyond the election cycle. There was no large youth groundswell speaking the language of Yuva Nyay. Like many Congress programmes, it was launched, discussed and eventually sank without a trace.

The Cockroach Janta Party began as a satirical, digital-first intervention with what old political parties lacked: irreverence, little legacy baggage and a vocabulary born on social media.

It gave accumulated frustration a conduit. Online anger over examination leaks spilled onto the street and widened into a protest over education costs, employment and institutional accountability. For Congress, this was the break it had spent years trying to manufacture but failed to produce.

Jha offers perhaps the sharpest explanation for why CJP succeeded where conventional opposition parties struggled.

The Modi government, he argues, can use agencies and the coercive power of the state to pressure political adversaries. It can also resort to what he calls âconvenient whatabouteryâ about 60 years of Congress rule. Students have fewer institutional or political stakes that can be turned against them, and familiar political labels do not work on them, according to Jha.

The challenge in front of Congress

The opposition, he says, failed to galvanise frustration that has now âerupted like a volcanoâ.

A party serious about youth politics, he asks, must also explain why the NSUI and Youth Congress were not present at Jantar Mantar in much larger numbers.

Political expert Subhamoy Maitra sees the emergence of figures like Abhijeet Dipke as evidence of a wider leadership crisis in mainstream political parties. Ashutosh Chatterjee, general secretary of the West Bengal Pradesh Congress and a former student leader, rejects that charge. Leaders are not âpropped upâ, he argues; those who consistently echo public sentiment eventually get recognition. He cites

Kanhaiya Kumar

, Manish Sharma and Vinod Jakhar among Congress's next generation and credits Rahul's

Chhatra Ki Goonj

with helping catalyse the student movement. He is categorical that there is no dearth of talent in Congress.

Rahul has meanwhile walked a tightrope with CJP, amplifying the issues, raising them in Parliament and meeting protesters while keeping a measured distance from Dipke and the core leadership. Congress wants to latch on to the momentum without getting directly associated with it, believes Maitra. Since the leaders of CJP are relatively unknown, he argues, it makes more sense for Rahul Gandhi to share a stage with the likes of AISA's Neha Bora.

With

Sonam Wangchuk

that Rahul Gandhi even declined to break his fast, it is clear that the Congress leader is trying to keep the protesters at arm's length.

Political scientist and former Calcutta University registrar Dr Rajagopal Dhar Chakraborti believes the NEET agitation was unusual because it organically brought sections of Gen Z together around a wider sense of institutional failure and caught the government off guard.

Students, he agrees with Jha, have little to lose and are harder to intimidate.

But Dr Chakraborti doubts Congress can simply inherit the dividend. CJP, he suggests, could eventually test the electoral waters itself rather than hand its constituency to any established party. He echoes the sentiments of Prashant Kishore that Bankipur result too is an indication of the mood inside the Gen Z constituents.

Jobs may be the bigger trigger

The World Bank estimates that around 11 million young Indians will enter the labour market every year over the next two decades.

Increasingly, the crisis is about the quality of employment, not just its availability. The gig economy cannot be a panacea for an increasingly educated and aspirational society. For decades, the implicit social contract was simple: a higher-education degree would culminate in a well-paying job.

That notion is now under stress.

AI, automation and other macroeconomic pressures could sharpen the mismatch. If India produces ever larger cohorts of graduates but a disproportionate share of new work remains temporary, informal or low-productivity, education itself could become a source of discontent.

Congress leader Chatterjee believes that the combination of unemployment, recurring paper leaks, shrinking space for public education and growing commercialisation of education will eventually push younger voters towards Congress.

He says Congress can offer Gen Z âtotal transparencyâ.

Can Congress states offer an alternative?

States do not control the entire macroeconomy, but they still have a large role to play in shaping the future of Indians, especially in areas like education, which is on the Constitution's Concurrent List.

Jha believes Congress needs an alternative model of governance where performance can speak for itself. He earmarks states like Karnataka and Kerala that could effectively be projected as models of governance.

But the inferno of student unrest has the potential to spill into opposition-ruled states, as Jharkhand is showing.

Congress is a partner in the JMM-led government, where students and government-job aspirants have protested alleged irregularities involving JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations.

Rahul Gandhi, to his credit, has addressed the issue head-on, describing the education system as having âcollapsedâ and become expensive and oppressive.

More importantly, he refused to exempt governments involving his own party, saying every government, including the one in Jharkhand, should listen to students and act.

From Rajiv's computers to Rahul's paper leaks

Congress has travelled this road before.

NSUI channelled students into party politics, and Youth Congress provided the next rung.

Rahul himself has spent almost two decades trying to build a younger political layer, with limited gains. Across large parts of India, the party remains top-heavy.

Dr Chakraborti turns almost wistful recalling how Rajiv enthused younger Indians before getting bogged down by a coterie of older Congress hands. Rajiv Gandhi once captured the young imagination far more successfully. In a pre-liberalisation India, computers and telecommunications became symbols of a future arriving early.

His government also lowered the voting age from 21 to 18.

The recent NEET debate in Parliament showed how Rahul and

Priyanka Gandhi

are operating. Rahul sought to legitimise student anger without claiming ownership of it. He told Parliament that Indians should be proud of the protesters, described students as people willing to question and keep their minds open, and called an expensive and commercialised education system an âextortion systemâ.

Priyanka spoke about injured students, asked whether protesters were âterroristsâ, and delivered a sharp line: if the prime minister wanted to win them back, he needed to change the âangle of his heartâ, not the camera angle.

Rahul Gandhi protesting in front of PM Modi's residence

Gen Z doesn't owe its vote to anyone

Political pundit Subhamoy Maitra offers the necessary caution.

It is far from clear, he says, how protest politics translates into electoral democracy. Barring movements such as Anna Hazare's anti-corruption agitation and the RG Kar protests, relatively few civil-society uprisings have produced durable electoral consequences in the last decade and a half.

He also believes Rahul still needs to shed the perception of being a âpart-time politicianâ. Chatterjee rejects that description, asking when a Leader of Opposition had previously had to shed blood while standing with protesters, as Rahul did during the NEET agitation.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

For all the marketing jargon, Gen Z is not one homogeneous political community. Caste, religion, region, class and gender will not disappear merely because everyone uses Instagram.

Students can welcome Rahul as an amplifier and still refuse to accept him as their leader. CJP has already shown that young Indians can organise outside both the ruling party and the established opposition. The party has already announced its next campaign " Kya Bolti Public".

Dr Chakraborti believes that this may well be a precursor to CJP testing waters in next year's Uttar Pradesh elections.

Gen Z content creators often harp on one word, which is consistency. That, they say, is what eventually produces organic reach. Rahul Gandhi might want to borrow the lesson, believes Sanjay Jha. Between Kalavati and Rhiya Ahir, Rahul Gandhi has toiled hard, often without much to show for it. Maybe that is because the party is yet to fundamentally establish how a Congress-ruled India would be different. That targeted messaging and, more importantly, tangible execution will be crucial.

Nearly 36 crore young Indians could be up for grabs in 2029. Sooner or later, they will ask what actually changed after they were heard.

World.title: 'Changing colours like a chameleon': Mayawati hits Akhilesh over 'Pandit' twist in SP's PDA formula
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

supremo

on Saturday launched a sharp attack on the

, accusing it of changing its political position for electoral gains after SP chief

Akhilesh Yadav

gave a new interpretation to the partyâs PDA formula.

BSP chief Mayawati alleged that the SP was now trying to attract Brahmin voters after noticing growing support for the BSP among upper-caste communities, particularly Brahmins.

Her remarks came after Akhilesh Yadav, while addressing a Brahmin Sammelan in Lucknow earlier this week, said the âPâ in the SPâs PDA formula -- Pichhde, Dalit, Alpsankhyak, could also stand for âPanditâ. He also accused the BJP government of targeting Brahmins.

In a post on X, Mayawati said, "As is well known, the

Bahujan Samaj Party

(BSP) is an Ambedkarite party dedicated to the welfare of all sections of society, implementing the policy and principle of 'Sarvajan Hitaya and Sarvajan Sukhaya,' and the four governments it formed in UP were also run on this very basis, whereas the Samajwadi Party (SP) keeps changing colours like a chameleon, openly and evidently, for the sake of its narrow casteist politics and electoral interests, etc."





Mayawati then took aim at the Akhilesh Yadav-led Samajwadi Party over its latest interpretation of the PDA formula, alleging that the party was changing the meaning of âPâ from âPichhdeâ to âPanditâ to attract Brahmin voters.

"In this very sequence, after first promoting 'P' in their so-called 'PDA'--meaning (Backward, Dalit, Minority)--as 'Pichhde' (Backward), now, upon seeing the upper-caste society, especially the Brahmin community, rapidly joining the BSP and party candidates being nominated on that very basis, the SP, feeling unsettled, has now changed 'P' to 'Pandit,' which is nothing short of another living proof of their political deception and trickery, if not, then what else is it?" the post read.

Mayawati also urged voters from all communities to remain alert against what she called the SPâs ânarrow casteist politicsâ. She argued that such strategies might bring short-term electoral gains but would not serve the interests of society as a whole.

Therefore, people from all sections of society must certainly remain vigilant against such a deceptive Samajwadi Party (SP) and its narrow casteist politics; this is the demand of the times and also in the interest of all sections of society," the post further read.

Akhilesh hailed his "Pichchde, Dalit, Adivasi -- PDA" formula after strongly denting BJP in Lok Sabha elections 2024.

World.title: 'Keep your curiosity alive': PM Modi addresses IIT Delhi graduates; highlights rapid tech shift
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday addressed IIT Delhi's 57th Convocation Ceremony, urging graduating students to embrace change, keep learning and remember the mentors who shaped their journey.

Addressing more than 3,000 graduating students, including 587 PhD scholars, as the chief guest, PM Modi congratulated them on completing their studies and asked them to embrace the next phase of their lives. "From orientation to convocation, you must be satisfied with your journey, but also excited about the start of a new chapter," Modi said.

He asked students to "live this moment to the fullest", noting that many were preparing to start their first jobs, move to new cities, launch startups or appear for competitive examinations.

The Prime Minister also urged them not to forget their time at IIT Delhi or the people who supported them. "Carry them as an asset; don't forget them. Before you leave, make sure to meet every member here," he said.

Speaking about the rapidly changing world and technology, the Prime Minister asked students to keep their curiosity and learning instinct alive.

"Today, the world is changing rapidly. Nobody can say what will happen 20-30 years from now.





Keep your curiosity alive in life... Keep your learning instinct alive. Those who learn, win," he said.

He said people who remain open to new situations and challenges can turn difficulties into opportunities. "Challenges become chances for those with courage to find new solutions," Modi said, adding that this was among the things students had learned at IIT Delhi.

"The global power balance is changing every moment and the biggest force behind it is the speed of technology," he said.

The PM also spoke about India's push for self-reliance and the emergence of new sectors for the country's youth. Referring to the semiconductor sector, he said India had begun production at its first semiconductor unit. "I firmly believe that from chips to ships, everything will be made here by your hands," he added.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The Prime Minister also presented IIT Delhi's top honours, including the President's Gold Medal, Director's Gold Medal, Shankar Dayal Sharma Gold Medal and Perfect Ten Gold Medals, to meritorious students.

He said he was proud of the graduating students but that there should have been "more" girls among them. "Just as your families are feeling proud today, I, too, am proud of all of you," he added.

Union Education Minister Prahlad Joshi, who was also present at the ceremony, said PM Modi's vision had made India's education ecosystem "learner-centric, research-driven, and future-ready".

Earlier, the Prime Minister inaugurated Param Pragya, an AI-powered high-performance supercomputing facility at IIT Delhi's Sonipat campus. According to the PMO, the facility will strengthen the institute's capabilities in AI, data science, advanced computing and interdisciplinary research.

World.title: Police conduct major search operation to check sale of ganja, tobacco products in Annamayya district
World.content:
More than 100 police personnel conducted an extensive cordon-and-search operation at Angallu village of Kurabalakota mandal in Annamayya district in the early hours of Saturday.

Speaking to the media, Superintendent of Police (SP) Dheeraj Kunubilli said that the special drive targeted suspected illegal activities, including the sale of ganja and narcotic substances. The SP said that the police teams had thoroughly searched streets and conducted checks at houses and other suspected locations in the village.

The searches were aimed to identify and crack down on groups allegedly involved in the sale and distribution of ganja and prohibited tobacco products.

“Vehicles without documents were also seized during the operation, and they would be subjected to verification,” the SP said.

“The extensive deployment of personnel and house-to-house checks created a heightened police presence in the village. The police stepped up efforts to curb alleged illegal activities centred around Angallu,” Mr. Kunubilli said.

World.title: Security guard found murdered at  farmhouse near Chittoor
World.content:
A 62-year-old security guard was found murdered at a farmhouse in Mangapuram village under Talambedu panchayat in Chittoor rural mandal on Saturday morning.

The deceased, identified as Anandaiah, had been working as a security guard at the farmhouse owned by Chinna Rajulu Naidu, who is currently residing in the U.S.

According to the police, other workers who arrived at the farmhouse for their routine duties found Anandaiah lying in a pool of blood. His throat had allegedly been slit with a sharp-edged weapon.

The Chittoor police rushed to the spot and cordoned off the area. A CLUES team was deployed to collect forensic evidence from the crime scene.

The motive for the murder was not immediately known. The body was shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital in Chittoor for postmortem examination.

The police said CCTV footage from the farmhouse and surrounding areas would be examined as part of the investigation. A case has been registered.

World.title: NIT-K ‘81 batch alumni present two electric buggies to alma mater
World.content:
Alumni of the National Institute of Technology-Karnataka (NIT-K), Surathkal, across multiple batches, returned to campus to mark the Institute’s 67th Foundation Day on Friday, with over 100 alumni from the 1981 batch alone joining the celebrations with their families.

The occasion saw the formal handover of two electric buggies to the campus under CAMPUS 81, a mobility initiative driven by the 1981 batch. CAMPUS 81 (Collaborative Alumni Mobility Partnership for University Sustainability) is an ongoing project under the CAMP (Contribute to Alma Mater Projects) programme, launched by the 1981 batch in 2018.

The initiative, with a total project cost of ₹17 lakh, comprises two electric buggies, a solar-powered charging facility and a GPS-enabled campus tour and information system, together forming a mobility ecosystem for the campus. The project was designed, fabricated, and led by U. Pruthviraj (associate professor and project coordinator of CAMPUS 81) and his team.

As part of the initiative, NIT-K has introduced CAMPUS 81 Electric Buggy to provide transportation for senior citizens, visitors, alumni, students and persons requiring mobility assistance. The buggies run on solar-generated power from the newly installed charging facility and will operate alongside the GPS-enabled tour and information system.

The project supports NIT-K’s broader goal of developing a sustainable, net-zero campus.

Present at the ceremony were B. Ravi, Director, NITK, Venkapayya Desai, Director, IIT Dharwad, D Prasanna Belur, Dean (Alumni and Corporate Relations), Mr. Pruthviraj and alumni representatives.

World.title: ‘Panthic’ politics: SAD-BJP renewed alliance could reignite Akali Dal’s core base ahead of 2027 Punjab polls
World.content:
Even as ‘Panthic’ politics, a political mobilisation surrounding the Sikh community’s collective identity, continues to be the cornerstone in Punjab’s electoral space, the restitching of an alliance between the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), could work in favour of the century-old SAD, which has been struggling to stage a political comeback in the State.

If the Akali Dal’s “core support base” sees a genuine prospect of returning to power in 2027, through this alliance with the BJP, that itself could become a rallying point drawing voters back to the SAD led by Sukhbir Singh Badal, who has served as Deputy Chief Minister in two separate stints.

Gradual downfall

Over the past decade, the SAD witnessed a gradual and significant downfall in Punjab’s politics, where Sikh identity and their issues have long been central to political discourse and different Akali groups have been fighting among themselves to capture the ‘Panthic’ space.

In 2025, the SAD saw a virtual split following the rebel faction forming a new outfit — Shiromani Akali Dal (Punar Surjit). Separately, the outfit ‘Waris Punjab De’ led by Lok Sabha MP and pro-Khalistan propagator Amritpal Singh, who is currently in Dibrugarh jail in Assam under the National Security Act, has been steadily building support within the ‘Panthic’ space, a trend observers link to the weakening of the SAD.

Another party, the SAD (Amritsar) led by Simranjit Singh Mann, a known hardline Sikh leader, has periodically stirred up Punjab’s electoral politics. Mr. Mann’s victory from Sangrur parliamentary constituency in the 2022 by-election pointed to the fragmentation within the ‘Panthic’ political space.

While the battle to garner ‘Panthic’ support among different political and other outfits has been going on, political observers feel the underlying strategic shifts amid speculation of a renewed SAD-BJP tie-up ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections could reshape the electoral landscape in the State.

Strong ‘tribal instinct’

Analysing the social engineering of Akali politics, Kehar Singh, former head of the Department of Political Science at Punjabi University, believes that the traditional agrarian Jat Sikh electorate functioning as the core support base of Akali Dal possesses a strong “tribal instinct” and maintaining unity within this core support base is inherently difficult without a viable path to authority.

“Power is the glue which can keep them together, otherwise, they’ll just split into various groups and different loyalties. If they see that there is any prospect of coming to power through an alliance with the BJP, it becomes an attraction point to rally around Sukhbir Singh Badal,” he said.

“Without an alliance, neither the BJP nor any individual Akali faction represents a standalone viable political option in Punjab. While formal announcements are yet to be made, a revived SAD-BJP partnership would fundamentally alter the dynamics of the upcoming contest in Punjab as their contesting individually would give an advantage to the Aam Aadmi Party and the Congress. Their joining hands will bring the SAD-BJP both into the reckoning,” he said.

World.title: Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation recovers 165 acres of its encroached land
World.content:
Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) has recovered 165 acres of its properties, which were encroached, over the last two years.

Lands recovered from encroachment during this period are in Hancharahalli (Mandur), Huchanapalya (Dasanapura), Hirandahalli (Hoskote), Totagere (Hesaraghatta), Kengeri, Bhyrathi and Kannur, among other places, BMTC said. The corporation also said it has registered 10 cases against 40 encroachers.

BMTC said that the drive was conducted with the coordination of multiple departments and will continue under the leadership of managing director and director (security and vigilance). BMTC said officials have been told to keep an eye on any encroachments and clear them at the earliest, apart from taking up measures to prevent any future encroachments.

World.title: Railway Board accords in-principle approval for BMRCL’s CBTC signalling system
World.content:
The Railway Board has accorded in-principle approval for the CBTC signalling and train control system for Namma Metro’s Pink Line (Reach-6) as well as the entire Blue Line – Phase 2A and 2B extending up to the Kempegowda International Airport.

The approval is an important milestone towards commissioning the Pink Line between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere.

Significantly, the same approval also covers the Blue Line from Central Silk Board to Kempegowda International Airport. While the signalling clearance was a pending milestone for the Pink Line, for the Blue Line, it has been secured well in advance of its proposed commissioning, facilitating timely testing and safety certification, said a release.

“For the Pink Line, BMRCL will now proceed with the remaining steps towards commencement of passenger services: interim speed certification from RDSO, statutory inspection of the rolling stock by CCRS, trial runs, and thereafter, the final statutory inspection and clearance for opening the line for public use,” said the release, adding that the BMRCL will continue to closely coordinate with all agencies concerned to complete these remaining processes at the earliest.

World.title: Annual Plan amendments approved for all local bodies in Kollam
World.content:
The District Planning Committee (Ad-hoc) has granted official approval for the annual Plan amendments across all 85 local self-government institutions in the district. The decision covers a network of local bodies, including 68 grama panchayats, 11 block panchayats, four municipalities, the district panchayat, and the Kollam Corporation.

District panchayat president R. Lathadevi has directed local authorities to take immediate steps to reduce spillover liabilities for projects approved by the planning committee for the 2026–27 financial year. She emphasised that priority has been assigned within the annual Plans to critical focus areas, including the Animal Birth Control (ABC) programme, scholarships for children with special needs, initiatives addressing school toilet shortages, and financial assistance for marriages and inter-caste marriages within SC/ST communities. She further urged local institutions that have allocated insufficient funds for the Jeevanam project to rectify the shortfall in the upcoming amendment cycle.

The committee has instructed the Kollam Corporation along with the Karunagappally, Kottarakkara, Punalur, and Paravur municipalities for completing and submitting their Plan amendments in a time-bound manner. Outlining the next operational steps, District Planning Officer Ullas J. said that projects receiving DPC clearance must undergo immediate technical vetting before transitioning directly to the implementation phase. He instructed local authorities to convene Grama Sabhas promptly to draft and finalize beneficiary lists for targeted schemes, ensuring these are submitted to implementing officers, while joint projects are forwarded directly to the respective block and district panchayats.

World.title: Welfare pension distribution in Kerala: Thomas Isaac seeks to roll back DBT decision
World.content:
Former Kerala Finance Minister T.M. Thomas Isaac on Saturday (August 8, 2026) demanded immediate roll-back of the United Democratic Front (UDF) government’s decision to shift welfare pension distribution fully to direct benefit transfer (DBT) mode. Dr. Isaac said that direct-to-home (DTH) distribution was chosen as an option as many of the pensioners had requested it.

Addressing a press conference, Dr. Isaac said that around 23 lakh beneficiaries had opted for the DTH mode so that they could get their monthly pension distributed to their homes via cooperative sector institutions.

When the Union government insisted on DBT for the payment of its share of the social security pensions, the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government had opted for that mode for 8 lakh beneficiaries who received a Central share in their payments. For the remaining beneficiaries, the pensions were either paid into their bank accounts via DBT or distributed to their homes depending on their choice, he said.

‘Baseless argument’

Now, the V.D. Satheesan government is upsetting this arrangement without even consulting the beneficiaries. The argument in the State government order that Kerala stood to lose Central financial assistance if the DBT was not implemented is baseless, Dr. Isaac alleged. The UDF government should urgently make public the Central government order in this regard, he said.

Further, the exemption for bedridden patients from mandatory DBT does not end the problem, he said. How can the government justify the denial of service to a beneficiary, who is not bedridden, who wants the pension distributed to his/her home, he asked.

Problems in the distribution by cooperative sector institutions, if any, should be resolved through discussion, Dr. Isaac said.

World.title: Rana Sanaullah says PML-N will form govt in AJK with two-thirds majority
World.content:
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Saturday that the PML-N would form the government in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) with a two-thirds majority.

He made the remarks while addressing a rally in Bagh ahead of the third phase of elections in the region. The third phase was originally slated to be held in the 11 constituencies of Poonch division, but will now only be held in its Bagh and Haveli districts due to law and order concerns.

Addressing the rally, Sanaullah said that in the first two phases, the PML-N had secured 24 seats. He said that six more seats were required for a two-thirds majority government.

Expressing confidence that the public will vote for his PML-N, the minister asserted that four more seats would be added following the August 10 polls, while five more would be added when polls would be held in the rest of Poonch Division.

“The PML-N will form a government with a two-thirds majority. The people of Kashmir have trusted PML-N. They have trusted Mian Nawaz Sharif. They have trusted the development in Punjab,” he said.

He urged supporters to show up and cast their votes on Monday to help PML-N secure a victory, promising that a PML-N government would prioritise development projects.

He also said that once in power, the PML-N government would meet with members of the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

“When this government will be set up, with a two-thirds majority, they will sit with [JAAC] representatives. Their first task will be to resolve this issue.”

He said that 99 per cent of JAAC protesters were “our brothers”, adding that they were patriotic Kashmiris and Pakistanis.

He added that the remainder were focused on creating divisions within the nation.

Sanaullah said India was trying to create misunderstandings between Pakistan and Kashmiris after failing to achieve its objectives through direct confrontation, adding that such attempts would never succeed.

He urged cooperation between a future PML-N government and the people of AJK in “exposing and defeating” those divisive elements.

“We will defeat them and we will make Kashmir prosperous,” Sanaullah said.

He further added that in the past, all large-scale development projects in AJK were only completed when the PML-N was in power in the Centre and in the region.

He urged the people of Bagh to go out and vote on Monday, stressing that “all of Bagh should be involved in the government”.

He added that PML-N founder Nawaz Sharif would fulfil his promises to the people of AJK by nominating one of the three PML-N candidates in Bagh as the future prime minister of AJK.

Sanaullah added that Nawaz has already mentioned that he would sit down with the future AJK prime minister to discuss development projects in the region.

Highlighting federal support, Sanaullah said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s government had approved a Rs23 billion special package for AJK in 2024 and provided wheat subsidy to facilitate the people.

He said the prime minister had also approved five Daanish Schools for AJK, while PML-N intended to take forward the public welfare and development model being pursued in Punjab.

World.title: Mir Raza Ali's body exhumed following restoration of original medical board
World.content:
The body of Institute of Business Administration (IBA) graduate and businessman Mir Raza Ali was exhumed on Saturday, his father’s lawyer said after the Sindh government restored the original medical board.

The exhumation had been scheduled for Friday morning but was postponed after Raza’s family objected to the abrupt reconstitution of a medical board and inclusion of members from outside Karachi division.

“The investigation officer was present when the body was exhumed and the examination was carried out. All eight people of the medical team were present; the parents were also nearby. And most importantly, a judicial magistrate … was present,” Advocate Jibran Nasir told the media in Karachi on Saturday.

The lawyer contended that “incomplete CCTV footage and out-of-context messages” have been used to ignite rumours and reach hasty conclusions since Raza’s death.

Raza, owner of eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28. The 25-year-old’s body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

While his family is convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, investigators probing the incident continue to build their case around the possibility that he died by suicide.

Commenting on the medical board controversy, Nasir expressed concern that the government did not provide any reason for changing the medical board overnight on Friday.

The lawyer said the victim’s family did not need “character certificates” for the doctors on the medical board.

He expressed hope that the medical board’s report would be received by Saturday evening, which would help clarify the circumstances of the young businessman’s death.

The report would clearly indicate if the incident was a murder or suicide, Nasir said, adding that the “police will be under even more pressure” once that question was cleared up.

“We hope we will have the answers to all these questions by 6pm today; whether it is self-inflicted or a murder,” he reiterated.

Nasir further said he was surprised to know that the police had shared audio evidence with the media before revealing it to the parents of the victim, who found out about it from TV reports.

Nasir expressed gratitude to the judiciary for intervening in the case, adding that “the work that police could not do in eight to nine days was done in two days after judicial intervention”.

Medical board controversy

The exhumation, which was scheduled for Friday morning, was postponed after the deceased’s family objected to the abrupt reconstitution of the medical board and inclusion of members from outside Karachi division.

On Thursday, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Raza’s father, Mir Hussain Ali, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation.

The court ruling came after a controversy emerged between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding the post-mortem examination.

Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed, whose assessment was based only on the post-mortem report and photographs as she had not examined the body herself, said some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with Dr Syed as the convener. Prof Dr Naseem Ahmed of Dow University of Health Sciences, Dr Farah Waseem of Jinnah Sindh Medical University, Amir Hassan Khan of Citizens Police Liaison Committee, Additional Police Surgeon Dr Sirichand, Dr Kamran Khan and Dr Daniyal Mirza of Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, and Dr Mohammed Yaseen, the admin in-charge of the police surgeon office, were the other members of the board.

However, in the early hours of Friday, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed to Prof Dr Zakiuddin from DUHS, Prof Dr Kazi Akbar and Prof Dr Abid Hussain Chang from Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences, and Hyderabad Police Surgeon Dr Waseem Khan.

On Friday morning, Raza’s family was present at the Tariq Road graveyard for the exhumation, which was then deferred.

Standing alongside Raza’s father, Nasir had accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts and held the police, health department and the Sindh government responsible for the delay.

World.title: OIC welcomes Pak-Saudi-Turkiye joint defence pact, calls it 'important strategic step'
World.content:
The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) has welcomed the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, terming it an “important strategic step”.

The pact aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers the three states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

In a statement posted on X, OIC Secretary General Hissein Brahim Taha expressed his “strong appreciation and support” for the agreement, describing it as an “important strategic step” that reflected the three countries’ commitment to strengthening regional and international cooperation.

Taha said the agreement constitutes “a fundamental pillar for supporting security and stability in the region and across the Muslim world”.

He added that it embodies a “shared resolve to address growing security challenges and strengthen solidarity and constructive partnerships” among the OIC member states.

The OIC is the second largest organisation after the United Nations, with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye among its 57 members.

The OIC chief also praised the “tireless efforts and wise leadership” of the three countries that culminated in the signing of the “historic agreement”.

He expressed hope that the pact would contribute to achieving peace and prosperity in the region and the wider international community.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed on Friday at a trilateral summit in Makkah, pledging to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan signed the pact during the “Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence”.

Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly has said the new tripartite agreement “does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries”.

Meanwhile, the Turkish president said the pact targets no country and remains open to participation of other friendly nations seeking peace.

PM Shehbaz undertook a three-day visit to Saudi Arabia from August 6 to 8, while Erdogan made a one-day trip to attend the summit.

On Saturday morning, the prime minister paid a visit to Masjid-i-Nabvi in Madina.

He then departed for Pakistan from the Madina airport, where he was seen off by Madina Governor Prince Salman bin Sultan Al Saud.

PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, also a former foreign minister, hailed the agreement as a “significant milestone” in the country’s history.

In a post on X, he noted that the pact was a “historic development that will further strengthen our defence capabilities”.

“This agreement is not only a guarantee of a stable and secure future for Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye, but also a historic document for regional and global peace,” he emphasised.

The PPP chairman also praised the roles of PM Shehbaz and CDF Munir “in making the agreement possible”.

Bahrain, Somalia welcome pact

In a statement issued by its foreign ministry, Bahrain welcomed the agreement as a “key addition to the broader regional defence architecture”.

Bahrain said it viewed the pact as a “strategic partnership between equal partners, driven by a shared commitment to safeguard regional and global stability while bolstering credible deterrence”.

The foreign ministry “highlighted the formidable defence capabilities and military expertise of the three nations, noting their proven track record in serving regional security, stability, and honouring international commitments”.

The pact “complements and enhances the collective defence systems of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) through solidarity and strategic integration”, Bahrain noted.

“Reaffirming that Saudi Arabia’s security is integral to its own, Bahrain expressed full support for all initiatives that protect national sovereignty, safeguard territorial integrity, and advance political solutions to regional issues,” the statement read.

Somalia, whose defence minister paid a visit to Pakistan earlier this week, also congratulated the three signatories.

In a statement, Somalia’s defence ministry termed the signing “a historic milestone in strengthening collective security, advancing defence cooperation, and building a strategic partnership capable of addressing shared security challenges”.

The ministry expressed confidence that the agreement “will make a significant contribution to enhancing regional peace and stability”.

While the signing of the agreement comes in the backdrop of heightened tensions in the Middle East arising from the US-Israel war on Iran, the pact was under deliberation months before the conflict began.

World.title: Pakistan, New Zealand seek to boost cooperation in agri, education sectors
World.content:
Pakistan and New Zealand discussed boosting cooperation in various fields, with a special focus on agriculture and education, as the two sides held a Joint Trade Committee (JTC) meeting in Wellington, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday.

The third Pakistan-New Zealand JTC meeting and the fifth round of Pakistan-New Zealand Political Consultations were held in Wellington on Thursday, “marking a significant step in deepening bilateral engagement between the two countries”, the FO said.

A key outcome of the meetings was the signing of the Education Cooperation Arrangement between Pakistan and New Zealand, which is “expected to significantly deepen collaboration in the education sector”.

At the JTC meeting, both sides “deliberated on improving market access and enhancing cooperation in sustainable agriculture, including exploring technical collaboration in wool production and plant protection”, the FO said.

The discussions focused on bolstering bilateral trade and investment, with particular emphasis on technology, education and services.

Institutional mechanisms to further economic cooperation were also discussed, the statement added.

Commerce Secretary Jawad Paul Khawaja represented Pakistan during the JTC meeting, while Grahame Morton, deputy secretary of the Americas and Asia Group at New Zealand’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, headed the other delegation.

Meanwhile, during the political consultations, both sides conducted a comprehensive review of bilateral relations. They also exchanged views on regional and international developments, and agreed to enhance coordination within multilateral forums.

Additional Foreign Secretary (Asia Pacific) Ambassador Dr Syed Ali Asad Gillani co-chaired the Pakistani side at the political consultations, while Morton headed the New Zealand delegation.

Islamabad and Wellington “explored avenues to strengthen cooperation across a wide spectrum of areas of mutual interest, including high-level exchanges, economic development, science and technology, education, counterterrorism, transnational crime, and people-to-people ties”, the FO said.

Ambassador Gillani briefed the New Zealand side on Pakistan’s efforts to de-escalate tensions in the Middle East, as Islamabad remains actively engaged in efforts to defuse the Strait of Hormuz stand-off.

Morton “acknowledged Pakistan’s constructive role in the Middle East peace process”, the FO statement said.

Gillani also discussed the situation in South Asia, including in India-occupied Kashmir (IoK) and India’s “continued violations” of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT).

India had unilaterally decided to put the IWT in abeyance in late April 2025 after hostilities flared up between the two neighbours last year. The issue of water has remained a bitter point of contention between the nuclear-armed nations since then, with Islamabad repeatedly raising the issue on international platforms.

The overall discussions between Pakistan and New Zealand “provided an opportunity to assess progress in bilateral ties, identify new areas for partnership, and reaffirm the shared commitment to a forward-looking and mutually beneficial relationship”, the FO noted.

Pakistan and New Zealand enjoy cordial and friendly relations, with both countries being members of the Commonwealth.

Bilateral trade stands at $12 million, with Pakistan’s major exports being textile products, apparel, rice, leather articles and sports goods, according to the FO’s website.

Main imports from New Zealand include dairy products, wood pulp, paper, edible oil, wood, iron steel and electrical machinery.

Agriculture and education were also among areas of cooperation discussed between the two sides when former military dictator Gen Pervez Musharraf visited Auckland in June 2005.

Last month, India and New Zealand signed a free trade deal as they sought to boost exports amid global economic uncertainty made worse by the war in the Middle East.

World.title: Heavy rain disrupts traffic, daily life in Lahore’s low-lying areas
World.content:
LAHORE: Heavy rain lashed Lahore on Saturday, inundating low-lying areas, major roads and several underpasses, making movement difficult for pedestrians and motorists in different parts of the city.

The downpour disrupted normal traffic as rainwater accumulated on roads and in low-lying localities, leaving motorists struggling to navigate waterlogged stretches.

Pedestrians also struggled to move through streets and roads where water had accumulated.

According to rainfall data from the Water and Sanitation Agency (Wasa), the city received an average of 24.6mm of rain.

The highest rainfall of 104mm was recorded at the airport, followed by 75.6mm at Kahna, 62.6mm at Hadiara Defence Road and 58.6mm at Manawan.

Tajpura sub-divisional officer’s (SDO) office recorded 40.2mm of rain, while 32.8mm was recorded at the Mughalpura SDO office.

Shadipura received 28.4mm, Nishter Town 28mm, Chowk Nakhuda 11mm, Johar Town SDO Office 11mm, while 10.8mm was recorded at the Wasa head office in Gulberg.

Upper Mall received 9mm, Samanabad SDO Office 4.4mm, Iqbal Town SDO Office 3.8mm, Saggian 3.8mm, Lakshmi Chowk 3.2mm, Jail Road 2mm, Gulshan-e-Ravi 1.8mm and Farrukhabad 1.4mm, while only trace rainfall was recorded at Pani Wala Talab.

Rain was also reported in Farrukhabad, Tajpura, Defence Phase-VI, Shadipura, Saggian, Lakshmi Chowk, Chowk Nakhuda and surrounding areas. Harbanspura and several other localities received heavy showers.

The rain brought relief from the heat and made the weather pleasant, but waterlogging in several areas caused inconvenience to residents and exposed the vulnerability of low-lying localities to heavy rainfall.

Meanwhile, Wasa Lahore said it had deployed field staff and machinery at various locations to drain accumulated rainwater.

Wasa Managing Director Ghufran Ahmed inspected drainage operations at Mubeen Shaheed Underpass, Noor Jehan Road, MM Alam Road, Main Boulevard Gulberg, Qaddafi Stadium and Liberty Chowk.

He also visited Kalma Chowk Underpass, Garden Town Water Tank, Usman Block Emergency Relief Camp and Usman Block Disposal Station.

Officials said drainage operations were continuing at waterlogged locations, with heavy machinery deployed in low-lying areas. Disposal stations in areas experiencing power outages were being operated on generators.

Wasa Vice Chairman Chaudhry Shehbaz Ahmed also inspected drainage operations at Shalimar Link Road, Bhagwanpura, Baghichi Sethan, UET, Ek Moriya, Do Moriya and Chowk Na Khuda.

Earlier, Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) Abdul Rahim Shirazi directed supervisory officers to remain in the field and monitor low-lying points and traffic conditions during the rainfall.

Traffic officials were directed to coordinate with Wasa for the timely drainage of rainwater from waterlogged locations.

Traffic police advised motorists to drive at moderate speeds, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles and avoid sudden braking on slippery roads. Motorcyclists were advised to wear helmets and avoid unnecessary overtaking.

Citizens were also advised to assess the depth of accumulated water before entering flooded roads and avoid crossing stretches where water levels were unsafe.

The traffic police warned citizens against standing near electric poles, transformers, fallen power lines, trees, weak walls and under-construction structures during rainfall.

World.title: Captain martyred, 7 terrorists killed in intelligence-based operation in Hangu: ISPR
World.content:
The military’s media affairs wing said on Saturday that a captain was martyred while seven terrorists were killed during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Hangu district.

In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said security forces conducted an IBO in Hangu on Friday following reports about the presence of terrorists belonging to Fitna al Khawarij — a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

During the operation, troops effectively engaged the terrorists, it said.

“In desperation, the khawarij took refuge inside a mosque, blatantly disregarding the sanctity of the place of worship. In ensuing fire exchange, seven khawarij belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khawarij were sent to hell,” it said.

The statement went on to say that during the exchange of fire, 27-year-old Captain Hamza Akram, a resident of Punjab’s Narowal district who was “leading his troops from front and relentlessly pursuing” the terrorists, embraced martyrdom.

“Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed khawarij, who remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities against the security forces and law enforcement agencies as well as killing of innocent civilians,” it said.

ISPR said that a sanitisation operation was being conducted to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored terrorists in the area.

President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the martyred captain, saying, “The motherland pays its profound tribute to the great sacrifice of its brave son.”

“The entire nation is indebted to the eternal sacrifices of these brave sons for the motherland,” the president added, offering prayers for the bereaved family.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed deep grief over Captain Akram’s martyrdom while hailing his courage and devotion, state-run APP reported.

In a statement issued by his office, PM Shehbaz lauded the security forces for eliminating seven terrorists “operating under the Indian patronage”.

“The nation will never forget the sacrifices of its brave sons,” the press release quoted him as saying. He prayed for the captain’s elevated ranks and for patience for his family.

The prime minister reiterated that operations against Fitna al Khawarij would continue till complete elimination of terrorism.

“The sacrifices rendered by our brave armed forces and law-enforcement agencies for the defence, peace and security of the country and nation will not go in vain,” he asserted.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also paid tribute to the martyred captain and offered his condolences to the bereaved family. He said that the officer had paid the ultimate sacrifice for the homeland and would remain alive in our hearts.

A day earlier, ISPR said 10 terrorists were killed in two separate engagements in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It said that in the first encounter, a group of terrorists attempted to attack security forces’ checkposts in Azam Warsak area in South Waziristan, which was effectively thwarted, resulting in the deaths of eight terrorists.

“In another encounter that took place in Dir district, own troops successfully neutralised two more khawarij,” it added.

Terrorist commander killed in Bannu

Separately, security forces killed a key terrorist commander, identified as Jamidullah, during an operation in Jani Khel area of KP’s Bannu district, a security official said.

The official said that the terrorist commander was involved in terrorist activities and was considered a quadcopter expert.

The official said that security forces conducted the operation in Jani Khel on the basis of intelligence reports, during which Jamidullah was targeted and killed.

World.title: Trump administration to invest $3 billion in minerals projects to boost US defence supply chains
World.content:
The US government will invest $3 billion in critical minerals and battery projects as part of a push to increase domestic production and boost national security and industrial policy, US President Donald Trump said on Friday.

“We’re reclaiming America’s rightful place as the minerals superpower of the world,” Trump told more than 200 mining executives, educators, investors and fellow politicians at a roundtable at the State Department aimed at supporting the industry, which he said had not received enough attention from Washington in recent years.

He announced a slew of investments during his speech, including a $1.4bn conditional loan from the Defence Department’s Office of Strategic Capital for Sila Nanotechnologies, which makes lithium-ion battery parts.

The OSC also extended a $400 million conditional loan to scandium miner Sunrise Energy Metals and a $150m conditional loan to magnet developer Niron Magnetics.

The US Export-Import Bank will lend $58m to Westwater Resources, Global Advanced Metals and 5E Advanced Materials, which Reuters reported earlier on Friday.

“Critical minerals are the raw materials of American strength that power everything from advanced weaponry to automobiles, and we want these essential products to be mined, refined and made right here in the USA,” Trump said.

Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and National Security Council official David Copley attended the announcement.

Weapons stockpiles drive mineral demand

The White House needs critical minerals to replenish weapons stockpiles depleted during the Iran conflict and reduce US dependence on Chinese supply chains.

Several executives came with gifts for Trump. Tom Albanese, chairman of deep-sea mining firm American Ocean Minerals, gave Trump a gold replica of a nodule that the company hopes to mine from the Pacific seabed. Trump last year said he may bypass the UN-backed International Seabed Authority and issue international seabed mining licenses.

Jim Litinsky, CEO of rare earths firm MP Materials, which is financially supported by the Pentagon, gave Trump magnets that had been produced for General Motors in the company’s Texas plant.

Other attendees included executives from Lithium Americas , which is building the largest US lithium mine, NioCorp, which is building a scandium mine to supply defence contractor Lockheed Martin, and Energy Fuels , which received a $725m OSC conditional loan in June.

US forces have burned through large numbers of precision-guided missiles and air-defence interceptors during the five-month-old US- Iran war. Defence officials and lawmakers have warned that replenishing some inventories could take years given existing production constraints. The Trump administration has disputed reports of significant shortages.

Supplies of minerals including rare earths, tungsten, germanium and scandium are essential for manufacturing precision-guided missiles, fighter aircraft, armored vehicles, infrared sensors and other advanced weapons systems, according to Pentagon officials and defence companies.

Mining schools receive funding boost

The Department of Energy on Friday hosted representatives from all 14 accredited US mining schools to promote mining careers and encourage more students to enter the field.

The department announced $100m in grants to help boost educational programs and set a goal of doubling the number of mining-related graduates at the nation’s universities within two years.

“We need to work on some systemic changes to how we as a nation want to offer our brightest students an opportunity to participate in this industry,” said Assistant Energy Secretary Audrey Robertson.

The Pentagon also said it would fund $80m in projects at three US mining schools.

Officials have pointed to China’s extensive network of mining universities as a key advantage in its dominance of global mineral production.

Since returning to office, Trump has launched a $12bn strategic minerals stockpile, backed equity investments in companies developing US mines and processing facilities, and sought to limit defence contractors’ reliance on supplies from China.

The administration says government support is needed to counter decades of Chinese investment that left Beijing dominant in the mining and processing of many strategic minerals.

Australia’s government on Saturday welcomed the Trump administration’s loan to Sunrise Energy Metals, which is developing a scandium mine in the country’s New South Wales state.

“The Sunrise Scandium Project hosts the world’s largest and highest-grade known scandium resource, which has a range of vital aerospace, defence and clean energy applications,” Resources Minister Madeleine King said in a statement.

World.title: Senate, NA leadership pledge closer cooperation for stable parliamentary system
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The leadership of the Senate and National Assembly on Saturday agreed to enhance institutional cooperation and coordination for a stable parliamentary democratic system.

According to a statement issued by the Senate Secretariat, Senate Chairman Yousuf Raza Gilani met National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq and Deputy Speaker Syed Ghulam Mustafa Shah at his residence.

The meeting focused on parliamentary affairs, matters of national importance and inter-institutional coordination, it said.

The Senate chairman said close coordination between the two Houses was indispensable for upholding “strong democratic traditions and an effective parliamentary system”.

He added that, “mutual cooperation and effective liaison between the Senate and the National Assembly were essential for the stability of the parliamentary system”.

Sadiq said institutional collaboration must be further strengthened for effective legislation and to meet public expectations, the statement said. The participants reaffirmed their commitment to making cooperation between the two Houses more effective.

During the meeting the leaders also held a detailed discussion on the overall situation in the country.

They agreed on the need to promote national interest, uphold the supremacy of the Constitution and advance democratic stability, the statement said.

The leaders reaffirmed their commitment to promote effective communication and mutual respect between parliamentary institutions and to further consolidate harmony and cooperation between the Senate and the National Assembly, the statement added.

A day earlier, Gilani inaugurated the newly modernised office complex of the Senate Secretariat at Parliament House, calling it a step towards institutional reform and strengthening parliamentary capacity.

Addressing the ceremony, he said, “strong democratic institutions required modern systems, efficient infrastructure and a professional working environment”.

He termed the upgradation part of a broader reform agenda aimed at improving service delivery and enabling the Secretariat to support Parliament in discharging its constitutional responsibilities.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.

If Bangladesh had 30–40 percent of the grid powered by solar, along with solar-powered EVs, the country would be far less exposed to global fuel market shocks. Long fuel lines, online schooling, shorter office hours, and industrial disruption could be reduced. Solar, storage, and EVs should now be planned together.

Finance will decide how fast this transition happens. Renewable energy projects cannot grow at interest rates below 10–12 percent. Long-term financing should be available at an interest rate of 3.5–4.5 percent. A 10–15-year financing facility at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent should be introduced.
