World.title: Won’t back down: Petty’s last laugh at Voss in Dees’ statement win; Bailey Smith shrugs off scandal in Cats’ win
World.content:
Loading

Melbourne backed born-again forward Harrison Petty for his gleeful take-down of former tormentor Patrick Voss on an afternoon that the Demons announced themselves as a serious premiership threat. Petty was a crucial key forward in the finals-like MCG clash, kicking three goals to help Melbourne down top-of-the-table Fremantle by four points – 17.11 (113) to 17.7 (109). Harrison Petty kicks three goals against Fremantle. Getty Images But it was after his first goal that he made his statement, rubbing his freshly shaved head in delight – an obvious broadside at Voss for his antagonistic treatment of Petty earlier this year. Following that round-two match at Optus Stadium, Voss was charged with misconduct and fined $1500 for mocking Petty by rubbing the then defender’s hair and simulating a crying action.



Related Article Updated

AFL 2026 ‘It’s not 1980 – the coach doesn’t run everything these days’: Scott speaks on concussion scandal It prompted the AFL to instruct umpires to start paying free kicks against players who rubbed the head of an opponent. But there was no taunting Petty on Saturday. He was crucial in the Demons’ fighting win – they trailed by three points a half-time, eight points at three-quarter-time and fell 15 points in arrears during a tense final term. Teammate Bailey Laurie, who kicked three valuable goals of his own, called Petty’s actions “awesome”. “Last time, I think he got his head rubbed, so I mean, he’s probably got the laugh today. So I’m sure he’ll be pretty happy with that one,” Laurie told The Age.



Coach Steven King was also full of praise for Petty. “I think it’s just him embracing who he is, being authentic. He’s on the big stage, you know,” King said. “[There’s] nothing wrong with shaving your head. I think it looks great. It wasn’t something I was aware that was going to happen. But I think that just shows where Petts is at. “He’s enjoying his footy. He’s proud of who he is, who he plays for, and yeah, it’s a good sign for him that he’s engaged in the game, and it means something to him.”



While Voss was at the opposite end of the ground to Petty, he was making a statement of a different kind. The damaging Dockers forward kicked four straight goals for the match. His teammate Jye Amiss also booted five without registering a behind. View post on X Their accuracy was unnerving for the Demons in an opening half that both sides piled on 21 goals between them in a mouth-watering shootout. At the long break, the Dockers led 11.2 to the Demons’ 10.5. “I think Kingy said we were plus-20 something in contest, and there were periods of the game we played really well, but we knew they were kicking all these goals that were pretty good. Like, tip your hat to them,” Laurie said.



“But all the stats were saying that if we kept doing what we were doing, we’d be right there at the end, which we were.” It was a game of fluctuating fortunes. Fremantle kicked four of the first five goals, Melbourne answered with the next four, the Dockers hit back with three in succession, and then Melbourne clawed their way back with four in a row. All this before half-time. Max Gawn has a fierce battle against Fremantle’s Luke Jackson at the MCG. Getty Images Then the midfields took turns in sharing dominance.



For most of the afternoon it was hard to split All-Australian ruck contenders and 2021 premiership teammates Max Gawn (16 disposals and 33 hitouts) as he did battle with Luke Jackson (17 disposals and 26 hitouts). “They’re both unique,” King said. “You could call both of them ‘unicorns’, I guess. Max has done things we haven’t seen. I think ‘Jacko’ now, the way he plays and follows up, he’s like an extra midfielder for them. Bailey Laurie celebrates the Demons’ win with coach Steven King. AFL Photos “I just think they’re both unbelievable footballers, and what a privilege it was to come here today to watch them both compete against each other.” The indefatigable Gawn played out the final term without a break as he willed his team over the line – they did not hit the front until the 21-minute mark of the final term on the back of a Bayley Fritsch snap.



But the Dockers had their chances. Jordan Clark and Matthew Johnson spilled marks in the last minute, while the enigmatic Fritsch was paid a mark right on the boundary line in the dying seconds that could easily have been ruled out-on-the full, allowing the Dockers one last roll of the dice. But none of that mattered to the Melbourne-dominated crowd of 40,938 who erupted in full voice as the final siren sounded. View post on X As they belted out the theme song, Fritsch kicked a behind, bumping the final margin to four points and bringing his total for the game to 2.5. Outside of Pickett, there were crucial bit-part players everywhere for the Demons who not only landed their biggest scalp of the season and improved their MCG record this year to 10-1, but have given themselves a chance at a top-four finish.



Tom Sparrow racked up 24 disposals and two goals, Koltyn Tholstrup blanketed the dangerous Murphy Reid, Harvey Langford took a mark-of-the-year contender, while hard-running wingman Harry Sharp managed three of his own, including a 60-metre bomb on the run from the boundary and a brilliant soccer goal in the pulsating final term. “I was saying to some of the boys throughout the game, as a spectator, that would have been unbelievable game to watch,” Laurie said. “To play my part in that was nice. It was very satisfying. We’re a special group, and anything’s possible.” King agreed, beaming with pride after winning a game at the MCG with a finals-like intensity against a team they rated as “the best team in it”. “I think for us it was a scalp we needed to take,” he said. “We needed to signify to the opposition that we’re here. We’re not just shooting to play a final. We want to make it count.“

- Danny Russell



Ollie Dempsey was again in standout form for the Cats. AFL Photos Young gun pushes his All-Australian claims Jon Pierik Star Geelong wingman Ollie Dempsey has put forward another case why he should be an All-Australian after helping the Cats to a 67-point win over Essendon at GMHBA Stadium on Saturday. Wearing his typical headband around his long blond locks, and dashing around in two different-coloured boots, Dempsey had 19 disposals and four goals, including a sharp snap in the second term after pouncing on a loose ball.



The win, including the percentage boost, ensures the Cats remain in the hunt for a top-four finish. They have North Melbourne and Richmond over the final two rounds. After a week of turbulence at the Cats given the Jake Kolodjashnij concussion scandal, superstar onballer Bailey Smith relished the chance to talk about anything but – heaping praise on Dempsey. “[He’s] All-Aus, surely. Just don’t take my wing spot. You can have the bench – just kidding,” Smith told Kayo Sports after the game. Dempsey said dismissed talk of an All-Australian nod but thanked those lobbying for him. “I’m not really thinking about it, it’s nice hearing all those things in public, but I’m just worried about getting the next two wins,” Dempsey told Kayo.



Related Article Updated

AFL 2026 ‘It’s not 1980 – the coach doesn’t run everything these days’: Scott speaks on concussion scandal The Cats quickly got to business against an opponent which initially was overwhelmed, but continued to fight, and reinforced that eventually there may be light at the end of the tunnel when a new coach is installed. The Bombers pressured as best they could, and had numbers around the ball. But they were goalless until just under two minutes remaining in the first half. They rallied in the third term, but the Cats cruised to their 10th-straight win over the red and black. Dempsey has the most goals of any wingman this season, his ability to slip forward causing rivals nightmares. He said he had not given any thought to earning a maiden green blazer. View post on X



“It’s always great fun playing at home,” Dempsey told Kayo Sports. Cats premiership great Tom Hawkins said Dempsey was a multi-faceted player. “He still gets back and defends, he is not just an attacking wingman. He supports the defence as well,” Hawkins said in commentary. Dempsey’s fellow forward Ollie Henry also booted four goals in a fine tandem act. Geelong pair Sam De Koning and Mark Blicavs shared the ruck duties, the former pushing forward when possible, but counterpart Vigo Visentini had a bagful of hitouts and was particularly impressive after half-time. He worked hard at stoppages and around the ground before leaving the field late after a heavy hit from behind. He, surely, will be a piece the new coach wants to harness.



Editor's pick Opinion

AFL 2026 The Cats are not the cultural beacon they once claimed to be Caroline Wilson Football columnist for The Age Veteran Cat Tom Stewart began in the middle at the opening throw-up, but spent most of the evening in his customary role of patrolling half-back. Smith’s excellent form continued. He was a metres-gained monster with 38 disposals, providing drive when the rain fell, while James Worpel and Tom Atkins provided grunt in close. Worpel could yet be under pressure should Max Holmes return from injury. The battle between impressive youngsters Nate Caddy and Connor O’Sullivan was one to watch, and something the football world will enjoy over the next decade. Caddy is a fighter and still wants the ball delivered to him no matter the strife his time is in. O’Sullivan had his moments in defence, this clash an even one. The Bombers have redeployed Zach Merrett back into his customary role in the midfield over the past month, and he was typically busy. In what could be his final weeks at the club, the former skipper had 29 disposals and 401 metres gained.



Sam Durham was quiet, but rookies Dyson Sharp, who found plenty of the ball, and Jacob Farrow, with two goals, continued their development. The Bombers host the Swans next Sunday, and could yet pinch one more victory, at home against Port Adelaide, to close what has been a largely dismal campaign. World.title: ‘Faceless’ foes to face off as Carlton and St Kilda scrap for wildcard spot
World.content:
Analysis SportAFLAFL 2026 ‘Faceless’ foes to face off as Carlton and St Kilda scrap for wildcard spot Peter Ryan August 8, 2026 — 8:36pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

There will be plenty of familiar faces on both sides when Carlton take on St Kilda at Marvel Stadium in what is arguably the most consequential clash between the two clubs since the 1972 preliminary final. Liam Stocker will be donning a Saints jumper for his 100th AFL game when he lines up alongside other ex-Blues Jack Silvagni and Tom De Koning, while former Saint Blake Acres will wear the No.13 Carlton jumper Stocker wore in his 28 matches with Carlton. Another win under interim coach Josh Fraser will kick the Blues two games clear of St Kilda in the race for a wildcard spot, while Ross Lyon’s team will leapfrog Carlton if they win – with a softer draw in their remaining two matches likely to see them home. St Kilda stars Tom De Koning and Jack Silvagni were huge names at Carlton before leaving the Blues as free agents. Getty Images It’s a huge game, particularly so for the Saints, who grabbed Carlton free agents De Koning and Silvagni during last year’s trade period to set them on a course for finals.



However, the animosity that existed between the two clubs in recent years as former Carlton list manager and club great Stephen Silvagni grabbed players from the list after an acrimonious departure from the club at the end of 2019 is said to have dissipated. Sources from both clubs, and former club officials who wanted to remain anonymous in order to speak freely, said there was no longer any angst towards each other, with the regime at Carlton now different from the one in place when Silvagni, Jack’s father, departed. While the Blues fought off an attempt to poach Brodie Kemp at the end of 2024, and weren’t happy to lose De Koning to such an outrageous offer last season, Silvagni was not a player they tried desperately to retain, despite his name being synonymous with the club. Josh Fraser has led the Blues to a 9-2 record since taking over as interim coach. AFL Photos A minor skirmish earlier this year, when the clearance of Carlton VFL player Ethan Phillips to St Kilda’s VFL list took longer than necessary, also showed the clubs were happy to play the game hard.



But when the two teams line up on Sunday evening a rivalry will be the furthest thing from their minds. “Every week it is about a faceless opponent, everyone builds up who you are playing, [but] your biggest opponent is yourself,” Lyon said after Silvagni and De Koning played against their former club for the first time in round eight. The two clubs have shared 46 players over their history, with former Blues Jack Carroll and Paddy Dow still on the Saints’ list, but they have hardly built a rivalry. The two teams have played against each other in just five finals, with the ’72 preliminary final their most recent. The Saints’ winning record of 26.75 per cent over Carlton is their lowest winning rate against any side in their history. In the late-1980s they tried to reverse that, with the Carlton crew consisting of premiership Blues Alex Marcou, Peter McConville and Ken Sheldon joining St Kilda at the end of their careers alongside other Blues Spiro Kourkoumelis, Warren Jones and Ricky Nixon.



Carlton great Alex Jesaulenko ended his playing career at the Saints The Age They had joined soon after the most famous Blue to become a Saint, Alex Jesaulenko, controversially joined the club in 1980 after coaching Carlton to a flag as captain-coach in 1979. None of the moves worked for the Saints, who spent that decade languishing at the bottom while the Blues kept playing in grand finals at winning flags. But the arrival of Carlton’s Aaron Hamill at Moorabbin in 2001 began to reverse that winning record, particularly at Marvel Stadium. The Saints now lead the head-to-head battle at that venue 22-8, with their two-point win over Carlton in the final round of 2024 tipping the Blues out of finals momentarily before Port Adelaide beat Fremantle later that day.



They defeated them comfortably earlier this season when the Blues, then coached by Michael Voss, suffered a familiar second-half collapse and Jack Silvagni showed he was on the path to an outstanding season. Sunday night is different. Lyon noted during the week Fraser has improved Carlton’s defence by six goals and jokingly nominated him for coach of the year for his effort in turning the Blues around. Fraser, for his part, was not getting caught up in any suggestions this game was anything other than business as usual – a game to win against a faceless opponent who had a talented bloke wearing No.7 (Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera) they had to worry about. “These are the games you want to play in,” Fraser said.



“These are the opportunities you want to be afforded. We’ve done enough to this point to have the opportunity to play in a game like this. We’ll lean into it, but it won’t be about the outcome – it’ll be the brand of football we want to play,” Fraser said. Nothing about the opposition. Nothing about the want to defeat the mob that contains a few of their former players. The process – that’s what Ross and Josh will focus on.

World.title: Buyer pays $2.91m for inner west semi for kids to live in while at uni
World.content:
PropertyNewsAuctions Buyer pays $2.91m for inner west semi for kids to live in while at uni Robyn Willis Updated August 8, 2026 — 8:32pm ,first published 1:08pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

A two-storey Erskineville semi sold for $2.91 million at auction on Saturday to an overseas buyer who the selling agent said had purchased it for his children to live in while studying at university. About 30 people, including several neighbours, gathered in the open-plan living area at the rear of 59A Prospect Street to witness the auction of the four-bedroom, three-bathroom architecturally designed home. The property had a guide of $2.5 million and sold for $260,000 above the reserve of $2.65 million. There is no legal requirement for a vendor’s reserve to be in line with their property’s price guide.



Six parties registered to bid, with bidding opening at $2.52 million. Two parties initially battled it out in increments of $10,000, $20,000 and $30,000. When bidding reached $2.65 million, two new bidders entered the fray, with 15 bid increases of similar sizes going back and forth between the two. A final bid of $5000 ended the spectacle with the underbidders, a couple with a child who own a property further west but rent locally, quietly saying “I think we’re out”. It was socks all round for the auction of 9A Prospect Road as a crowd assembled in the compact open-plan living area. James Brickwood A lawyer acting on behalf of the successful bidder said his client was based overseas. Records show the property on the 144-square-metre site last sold in 2016 for $1.92 million. The property was one of 520 scheduled to go to auction in Sydney this week. By evening, Domain Group recorded a preliminary auction clearance rate of 50 per cent from 292 reported results throughout the week, while 94 auctions were withdrawn.





The landscaped backyard at the rear of 59A Prospect Street. Domain One of the vendors, who was present at the auction, said that while it was “very difficult to move” because her family had enjoyed the close-knit local community, an “outstanding” property closer to the city had convinced them to make a fresh start, so they bought it. In Lane Cove, a local family with a young child paid $1,463,000 for a three-bedroom apartment after it passed in at auction on Saturday. Bidding for the property at 2/15 Longueville Road opened at $1.38 million, increasing in bids of $10,000 to reach $1.45 million when things stalled and it passed in. The lead bidder was then invited to increase their offer and, after half an hour of negotiating, the property sold.



The apartment had a guide of $1.4 million and a reserve of $1.5 million. Related Article Sydney house prices ‘Fewer buyers’: The Sydney suburbs with the deepest property downturns Two bidders registered, although Raine & Horne Lower North Shore sales agent Oscar Nicholls was initially expecting only one. The underbidder was an investor who had seen the property once early in the campaign and was attracted to it for its yield potential, Nicholls said. “He got to a point [in the bidding] and said ‘at this price point it doesn’t make any sense’. He has a couple of investments which he is holding because rents are up,” Nicholls said. The vendor was a single-parent family who bought a four-bedroom home. Nicholls said market conditions were good for upsizers.



“She got a really good deal on what she bought,” he said of the new property. The three-bedroom apartment has two bathrooms, a double garage and a living area opening onto a private courtyard. Domain In Bondi Junction, negotiations continued after a two-bedroom art deco apartment passed in at $775,000. Two parties registered to bid for 2/143 Old South Head Road but just a single bid of $750,000 was placed when the auction opened. The lead bidder, a first home buyer renting in Paddington, was invited to advance on their offer with a further bid of $775,000 before the property passed in.



The apartment, sold as a deceased estate, had a guide of $800,0000 and a reserve of $850,000. It is one of nine apartments in a block positioned between Bellevue Hill and Bondi Junction and features high ornate ceilings, timber fretwork and picture rails, typical of the era. The art deco apartment is one of just nine in the boutique block. Domain A sales agent for Ray White Eastern Beaches, Angus Gorrie, expects the property to sell next week. “It takes a bit more time [to sell in this market], but we had two registered buyers, and we are getting close,” he said. “People are out there – the market is better than it was in June.”

World.title: Sheer lunacy and a coming of age: Inside the greatest Battle of Brisbane yet
World.content:
SportNRLNRL 2026 Sheer lunacy and a coming of age: Inside the greatest Battle of Brisbane yet Nick Wright August 8, 2026 — 7:55pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Jot it down and remember where you were for the craziest Battle of Brisbane yet. It may have been the Dolphins who took home the two points in a thrilling 40-32 shootout against the Broncos – securing their maiden finals appearance in the process – but the 50,000-plus fans who packed into Suncorp Stadium were arguably the biggest winners of Saturday night. Selwyn Cobbo scores for the Dolphins on Saturday. Getty Images There were moments of brilliance and sheer lunacy, contract statements and ominous reminders, injury scares and flaring tempers. As Broncos coach Michael Maguire said, “it was an unusual game”. It might be best if we just broke it down.



Mam magic and a contract statement Ezra Mam has been a man maligned for much of season 2026 – his axing at times throughout the campaign symbolic of the Broncos’ dramatic slide from defending champions to the doldrums of the competition. But the under-siege five-eighth issued a stunning reminder of just what he could produce with a first-half hat-trick that threatened to completely take the game away from the Dolphins. Loading It was fitting that in Indigenous Round Mam produced his finest performance of the year, his first highlight bouncing on the outside of Reece Walsh to take his fullback’s pass and score untouched from close range. The opportunity came from a Billy Walters 40/20, it what was the off-contract hooker’s first starting appearance since rupturing his ACL last year.



“It’s a testament to all Bill’s hard work, it would have been tough sitting in his position last year, and to fight his way through it … he’s earned his spot,” Broncos skipper Pat Carrigan said. “The Walters name is synonymous with the club, and he lives and breathes what it’s like to play for the Broncos – I’m really proud of him and a bit disappointed we couldn’t get the win for his 100th game.” For Mam’s next trick, shortly after Jamayne Isaako sent the Dolphins’ kick-off out on the full, the 23-year-old simply ran it hard and straight at the defence, before shrugging off a pair of tackles and reaching out desperately for his second. Walters was quick to issue another reminder of why he must be retained at Red Hill, slicing out of dummy half and splitting the defence, before finding Deine Mariner on his inside to score an 80-minute special. It was then Mam’s kicking game which extended Brisbane’s early lead to 24 points, his grubber twice fumbled by Jack Bostock for Xavier Willison to touch down.



And even after the Dolphins scored three straight tries, it was Mam who wrestled back the ascendancy for a moment – scoring straight from a scrum after Tom Gilbert’s knock on. Just as he was in the 2023 grand final, Mam appeared destined to add a man of the match medal to his accolades. Until one moment and a rival general flipped the script. The good fortune and little general The Dolphins needed something to go their way as Mam orchestrated a 24-0 Broncos lead. Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow was on hand to provide that. As the Broncos went on the attack again, a dropped ball by Jaiyden Hunt was swooped on by the Dolphins’ No.1 – his smile as soon as he grabbed possession a sign he knew he would not be caught on the 90-metre dash to score.



Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow scores against Brisbane. Getty Images While that try may have been in fortuitous circumstances, it appeared to awaken his side as they hunted to keep their top four hopes alive. From the following set, Max Plath – who was outstanding all night, finishing with 184 running metres – burst through the middle and into the clear to go deep into Brisbane territory. Halfback Isaiya Katoa then stood up, commanding his team into position for him to fire a perfect short pass for Connelly Lemuelu to cut the deficit to 12 points. Katoa was at it again when the Dolphins clinched the momentum, with the 22-year-old’s brilliant face pass for Bostock presenting a two-on-one, with Isaako finishing the job in the corner.



While Mam’s third briefly halted the surge, it would not be for long. Ben Talty’s dropped ball coming out of trouble opened the door, and the Dolphins turned globetrotters. Winger Selwyn Cobbo could have panicked when Katoa’s attempted long ball went behind him and crept towards the sideline, but the former Bronco’s tap-back for a supporting Farnworth was perfect. The England centre was then hardly troubled on his way to the line, the Broncos’ defence parting without hesitation. Somehow, at half-time, the Dolphins led 30-24. “Key moments are hurting us, that’s where we’re at,” Maguire lamented. “Obviously, I’m frustrated, you can’t leak or let in that many tries to put yourself in a position to really contend.”



Katoa’s masterclass and ‘The Hammer’s’ miracle He had shown signs he was about to make this game his own, but it was the way Katoa controlled the second half which ultimately proved the difference. The first-half shootout had quickly descended into an arm wrestle, with Mariner and Gilbert both sent for head injury assessments, and Farnworth seen limping regularly after an awkward tackle on his lower leg by opposite number Kotoni Staggs. Against a Broncos side missing skipper and veteran halfback Adam Reynolds, it was Katoa’s composure which guided the Dolphins home – relying on his patient kicking game while waiting for his moment to strike. That chance came when Tabuai-Fidow’s kick return, and Plath’s bulldozing carry with three defenders on his back, got the Redcliffe army on the charge – Katoa’s delicate chip over the top gifting Lemuelu his second try of the night.



Related Article NRL 2026 Rabbitohs deny Eels greatest comeback in NRL history While Walsh would ice a penalty goal to earn Brisbane the lead back, Katoa was far from finished with the boot. His attacking bomb was miraculously taken by Tabuai-Fidow, who reached out to score his second and clinch the lead, before the Tongan maestro’s cross-field effort was reeled in by Bostock and eventually spread back the other way for Cobbo to seal the win. “It’s something I’ve been working on, and I think I can get over a couple of fullbacks. I looked at Issy and just said ‘iso’ [isolated kick] … I got the try, it’s pretty cool,” Tabuai-Fidow relived. By full-time, for all of the individual brilliance Mam and Tabuai-Fidow showcased, Katoa was the evening’s mastermind – orchestrating five of his side’s seven tries.



“You could see we had our attack on, you could see we were going to find opportunities – we were making little half breaks and linebreaks, and that gave me a lot of confidence,” Dolphins coach Kristian Woolf said. “I do love the way he steered the ship, he’s our leader and halfback, he’s got a great temperament on him, and I thought he controlled that second half really well.”

World.title: Mistakes abound, but Wallabies’ win provides plenty of satisfaction
World.content:
SportRugby UnionWallabies Opinion Mistakes abound, but Wallabies’ win provides plenty of satisfaction Peter FitzSimons Columnist and author August 8, 2026 — 11:00pm

August 8, 2026 — 11:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Get that up yer, Eddie. The Wallaby win over Japan in Osaka was satisfying on a dozen levels at once. Most importantly, of course, is the fact that it was indeed a WIN, a victory if not a triumph, but that rarest of breed in recent times, a (W) next to the Wallaby name on the scoring ledger as the final whistle blew. And it was terrific that it came in the first match of new Wallaby coach Les Kiss’s tenure. The Wallabies’ lineouts were excellent, and Josh Canham turned in a near Man of the Match performance. Getty Images But right up there in terms of satisfaction was that it was against a side coached by Eddie Jones, who in fact was negotiating to take that very position while having carriage of the Australian team in the 2023 World Cup. The result was that our side was a complete shambles, and he left behind the smoking ruins of what might have been.



But here, three years later, our blokes registered a small payback against a Japanese side good enough to have easily defeated Italy and even threatened Ireland in recent times. The win to the Goodies, came despite several things not going the Wallabies’ way. The first thing was playing in such heat and humidity; it was clear from the first that in terms of sheer energy expended, not to mention hugely skilful play, the habituated locals were always going to be a handful. We were also a man down for twenty minutes – following lock Miles Amatosero being dispatched for high contact - which exhausted the surviving fourteen further. And finally, we had an error rate that would kill a brown dog. Balls were kicked out on the full, knocked on and dropped behind with alarming regularity, even while the Japanese kicks were twice allowed to bounce and we kept making mistakes just when the try-line beckoned. Against that? Ryan Lonergan kicks the ball. Getty Images



Well, against that both our scrum and lineouts were excellent, and the surviving lock, Josh Canham – sort of rhymes with CANNON - turned in a near Man of the Match performance, stealing balls in the lineout, winning his own, ripping the balls off them in the maul, and constantly penetrating their line with death-or-glory charges. In the back row, Fraser McReight had his usual strong game while, off the bench, Taniela Tupou scored a great try which – if I were him – I’d describe as “a 50-metre carry, sidestepping my way through,” but was closer to a five-centimetre carry, followed by falling over the line with the ball in hand. The point was, after marvellous lead-up work by the entire team, it was Tupou who was there at the death to finish the job against a valiant Cherry Blossoms team that simply refused to quit. It was also Tupou who pulled off a massive tackle at the death, making his opponent spill the ball, which finally put the game to rest. Angus Bell also had a great game off the bench, as did Jeremy Williams, and in some ways Kiss’s bench might have been stronger than the starting side they replaced, which saw the Wallabies finish strongly and not fade badly, which they have also been wont to do in recent times. Related Article Live

Wallabies Wallabies go down to the wire in tight victory over Japan In our back-line we saw the virtues of new coach Les Kiss’s stated desire to have less structured play, to have his charges work less with zones and channels and more with – stop me if this is too complex – running to where the bloody gaps are! Time and again they did that, led by Max Jorgensen, and the results were there for all to see. The diminutive winger – and Tom Wright at fullback – were standouts for us, while the other winger Harry Potter had another strong game, as did Ryan Lonergan at halfback. When Tate McDermott came on to replace him at half in the final twenty minutes, he did what he does best, launching a series of darting runs from the base of the scrums, rucks and mauls and always laying the ball back.



At fly-half, Declan Meredith struggled, and it was frankly a surprise that he played the full eighty minutes, as hard as he did try. (Carter Gordon, who was a revelation against Ireland last month, before injuring himself, will likely be back next week, in the return bout against Japan in Townsville.) Joseph Suaalii also struggled at times to hold on to the ball, though as captain Harry Wilson noted at game’s end, in those conditions the ball was like soap. Whatever. It was a WIN, did I mention? And not only that, the Wallabies second in succession! Get that up yer, Eddie. News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport sent every Monday.

World.title: Rabbitohs deny Eels greatest comeback in NRL history
World.content:
SportNRLNRL 2026 Rabbitohs deny Eels greatest comeback in NRL history Jasper Bruce and Justin Chadwick Updated August 8, 2026 — 10:12pm ,first published 5:33pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Parramatta have come within a sliver of the greatest comeback in NRL history, but have gone down 28-24 to South Sydney, who moved one step closer to a top-eight finish. But the manic victory looks to have come at a cost as young Souths halfback Ashton Ward injured his hamstring attempting a sideline conversion in Saturday’s first half. Loading Alex Johnston crossed for three tries as Souths took an imperious 28-0 halftime lead in the veteran winger’s first game at Allianz Stadium since breaking the NRL’s tryscoring record. The Eels lost Brian Kelly to the sin bin for a professional foul after just 92 seconds and conceded three tries without him, then watched as gun fullback Isaiah Iongi went down with a knee injury just before the break.



But against all odds, and with no realistic finals hopes to play for, Parramatta were hoisted back into the contest by off-contract journeyman Ronald Volkman. Ronald Volkman celebrates a try. Getty Images With Josh Addo-Carr deputising at fullback and hooker Ryley Smith in the centres, five-eighth Volkman’s attacking nous threatened to help the Eels pass the standing record for biggest NRL comeback (26 points). After Tallyn Da Silva crossed for the Eels’ first try, Volkman kicked through for Smith to nab their second before spinning past Matt Dufty for a four-pointer of his own. When Jordan Samrani soared over makeshift winger Jye Gray and slammed Volkman’s kick down, Parramatta were within four points.



After forcing a dropout in the final minutes, the Eels looked set to go for the killer blow, but the returning Tallis Duncan regathered the Rabbitohs’ short restart. In the same set, veteran Cody Walker kicked a 40/20 to put Souths out of trouble and on the attack for the final exchanges of a calamitous game. Brandon Smith celebrates a Rabbitohs try. Getty Images In Indigenous Round, Walker had been integral to the Rabbitohs’ early lead, most memorably slamming a kick into the goalposts that Tevita Tatola regathered for a fantastic try. The win lifts Souths back into seventh place to finish a weekend during which top-eight rivals Manly and Canterbury suffered potentially costly defeats.



They will likely make finals if they win two of their remaining four games, but have tough matches against Canterbury, the Warriors and Sydney Roosters on the run home. Earlier, Manly endured a dark day in Perth, conceding a whopping 42 consecutive points as their finals hopes took an almighty hit in a 42-20 loss to Melbourne. The Storm were horrible early on Saturday, with their completion rate sitting at just five of 12 as the Sea Eagles scored the opening two tries of the match to race out to a 14-0 lead. Loading But it was all one way traffic from that point on, with Melbourne piling on six unanswered tries either side of half-time to turn the contest on its head.



Manly’s fifth loss on the trot leaves their finals hopes on life support. Kieran Foran’s men now nurse a 9-11 record, meaning they will have to win their last four games to have a legitimate chance of making finals. In a further blow for the Sea Eagles, prop Taniela Paseka limped off in the first half after suffering a suspected MCL injury. Sualauvi Fa’alogo celebrates a try for Melbourne. Getty Images The Storm snapped a three-game losing streak, but at 9-12 they need to win their remaining three games and rely on other results to go their way in order to sneak into the post-season.



Fittingly, Melbourne’s Nick Meaney was a perfect nine-of-nine with the boot in a place he will soon call home. Related Article Updated

NRL 2026 NRL gives Perth Bears cap concessions to boost marquee pitch as inaugural jersey revealed The centre will join Perth next season and there were plenty of Bears fans in attendance to watch their future star. Perth coach Mal Meninga led around 1000 supporters on a pre-match ‘Bear Walk’ in the rain to HBF Park to signify the venue will soon become a ‘Bear Pit’. The NRL’s newest franchise launched their home jersey on Friday, with the red-and-black hooped strip paying tribute to the first-ever North Sydney Bears side of 1908, when the club was a foundation member of the NSW Rugby Football League. World.title: Won’t back down: Petty’s last laugh at Voss in Dees’ statement win; Bailey Smith shrugs off scandal in Cats’ win
World.content:
Loading

Melbourne backed born-again forward Harrison Petty for his gleeful take-down of former tormentor Patrick Voss on an afternoon that the Demons announced themselves as a serious premiership threat. Petty was a crucial key forward in the finals-like MCG clash, kicking three goals to help Melbourne down top-of-the-table Fremantle by four points – 17.11 (113) to 17.7 (109). Harrison Petty kicks three goals against Fremantle. Getty Images But it was after his first goal that he made his statement, rubbing his freshly shaved head in delight – an obvious broadside at Voss for his antagonistic treatment of Petty earlier this year. Following that round-two match at Optus Stadium, Voss was charged with misconduct and fined $1500 for mocking Petty by rubbing the then defender’s hair and simulating a crying action.



Related Article Updated

AFL 2026 ‘It’s not 1980 – the coach doesn’t run everything these days’: Scott speaks on concussion scandal It prompted the AFL to instruct umpires to start paying free kicks against players who rubbed the head of an opponent. But there was no taunting Petty on Saturday. He was crucial in the Demons’ fighting win – they trailed by three points a half-time, eight points at three-quarter-time and fell 15 points in arrears during a tense final term. Teammate Bailey Laurie, who kicked three valuable goals of his own, called Petty’s actions “awesome”. “Last time, I think he got his head rubbed, so I mean, he’s probably got the laugh today. So I’m sure he’ll be pretty happy with that one,” Laurie told The Age.



Coach Steven King was also full of praise for Petty. “I think it’s just him embracing who he is, being authentic. He’s on the big stage, you know,” King said. “[There’s] nothing wrong with shaving your head. I think it looks great. It wasn’t something I was aware that was going to happen. But I think that just shows where Petts is at. “He’s enjoying his footy. He’s proud of who he is, who he plays for, and yeah, it’s a good sign for him that he’s engaged in the game, and it means something to him.”



While Voss was at the opposite end of the ground to Petty, he was making a statement of a different kind. The damaging Dockers forward kicked four straight goals for the match. His teammate Jye Amiss also booted five without registering a behind. View post on X Their accuracy was unnerving for the Demons in an opening half that both sides piled on 21 goals between them in a mouth-watering shootout. At the long break, the Dockers led 11.2 to the Demons’ 10.5. “I think Kingy said we were plus-20 something in contest, and there were periods of the game we played really well, but we knew they were kicking all these goals that were pretty good. Like, tip your hat to them,” Laurie said.



“But all the stats were saying that if we kept doing what we were doing, we’d be right there at the end, which we were.” It was a game of fluctuating fortunes. Fremantle kicked four of the first five goals, Melbourne answered with the next four, the Dockers hit back with three in succession, and then Melbourne clawed their way back with four in a row. All this before half-time. Max Gawn has a fierce battle against Fremantle’s Luke Jackson at the MCG. Getty Images Then the midfields took turns in sharing dominance.



For most of the afternoon it was hard to split All-Australian ruck contenders and 2021 premiership teammates Max Gawn (16 disposals and 33 hitouts) as he did battle with Luke Jackson (17 disposals and 26 hitouts). “They’re both unique,” King said. “You could call both of them ‘unicorns’, I guess. Max has done things we haven’t seen. I think ‘Jacko’ now, the way he plays and follows up, he’s like an extra midfielder for them. Bailey Laurie celebrates the Demons’ win with coach Steven King. AFL Photos “I just think they’re both unbelievable footballers, and what a privilege it was to come here today to watch them both compete against each other.” The indefatigable Gawn played out the final term without a break as he willed his team over the line – they did not hit the front until the 21-minute mark of the final term on the back of a Bayley Fritsch snap.



But the Dockers had their chances. Jordan Clark and Matthew Johnson spilled marks in the last minute, while the enigmatic Fritsch was paid a mark right on the boundary line in the dying seconds that could easily have been ruled out-on-the full, allowing the Dockers one last roll of the dice. But none of that mattered to the Melbourne-dominated crowd of 40,938 who erupted in full voice as the final siren sounded. View post on X As they belted out the theme song, Fritsch kicked a behind, bumping the final margin to four points and bringing his total for the game to 2.5. Outside of Pickett, there were crucial bit-part players everywhere for the Demons who not only landed their biggest scalp of the season and improved their MCG record this year to 10-1, but have given themselves a chance at a top-four finish.



Tom Sparrow racked up 24 disposals and two goals, Koltyn Tholstrup blanketed the dangerous Murphy Reid, Harvey Langford took a mark-of-the-year contender, while hard-running wingman Harry Sharp managed three of his own, including a 60-metre bomb on the run from the boundary and a brilliant soccer goal in the pulsating final term. “I was saying to some of the boys throughout the game, as a spectator, that would have been unbelievable game to watch,” Laurie said. “To play my part in that was nice. It was very satisfying. We’re a special group, and anything’s possible.” King agreed, beaming with pride after winning a game at the MCG with a finals-like intensity against a team they rated as “the best team in it”. “I think for us it was a scalp we needed to take,” he said. “We needed to signify to the opposition that we’re here. We’re not just shooting to play a final. We want to make it count.“

- Danny Russell



Ollie Dempsey was again in standout form for the Cats. AFL Photos Young gun pushes his All-Australian claims Jon Pierik Star Geelong wingman Ollie Dempsey has put forward another case why he should be an All-Australian after helping the Cats to a 67-point win over Essendon at GMHBA Stadium on Saturday. Wearing his typical headband around his long blond locks, and dashing around in two different-coloured boots, Dempsey had 19 disposals and four goals, including a sharp snap in the second term after pouncing on a loose ball.



The win, including the percentage boost, ensures the Cats remain in the hunt for a top-four finish. They have North Melbourne and Richmond over the final two rounds. After a week of turbulence at the Cats given the Jake Kolodjashnij concussion scandal, superstar onballer Bailey Smith relished the chance to talk about anything but – heaping praise on Dempsey. “[He’s] All-Aus, surely. Just don’t take my wing spot. You can have the bench – just kidding,” Smith told Kayo Sports after the game. Dempsey said dismissed talk of an All-Australian nod but thanked those lobbying for him. “I’m not really thinking about it, it’s nice hearing all those things in public, but I’m just worried about getting the next two wins,” Dempsey told Kayo.



Related Article Updated

AFL 2026 ‘It’s not 1980 – the coach doesn’t run everything these days’: Scott speaks on concussion scandal The Cats quickly got to business against an opponent which initially was overwhelmed, but continued to fight, and reinforced that eventually there may be light at the end of the tunnel when a new coach is installed. The Bombers pressured as best they could, and had numbers around the ball. But they were goalless until just under two minutes remaining in the first half. They rallied in the third term, but the Cats cruised to their 10th-straight win over the red and black. Dempsey has the most goals of any wingman this season, his ability to slip forward causing rivals nightmares. He said he had not given any thought to earning a maiden green blazer. View post on X



“It’s always great fun playing at home,” Dempsey told Kayo Sports. Cats premiership great Tom Hawkins said Dempsey was a multi-faceted player. “He still gets back and defends, he is not just an attacking wingman. He supports the defence as well,” Hawkins said in commentary. Dempsey’s fellow forward Ollie Henry also booted four goals in a fine tandem act. Geelong pair Sam De Koning and Mark Blicavs shared the ruck duties, the former pushing forward when possible, but counterpart Vigo Visentini had a bagful of hitouts and was particularly impressive after half-time. He worked hard at stoppages and around the ground before leaving the field late after a heavy hit from behind. He, surely, will be a piece the new coach wants to harness.



Editor's pick Opinion

AFL 2026 The Cats are not the cultural beacon they once claimed to be Caroline Wilson Football columnist for The Age Veteran Cat Tom Stewart began in the middle at the opening throw-up, but spent most of the evening in his customary role of patrolling half-back. Smith’s excellent form continued. He was a metres-gained monster with 38 disposals, providing drive when the rain fell, while James Worpel and Tom Atkins provided grunt in close. Worpel could yet be under pressure should Max Holmes return from injury. The battle between impressive youngsters Nate Caddy and Connor O’Sullivan was one to watch, and something the football world will enjoy over the next decade. Caddy is a fighter and still wants the ball delivered to him no matter the strife his time is in. O’Sullivan had his moments in defence, this clash an even one. The Bombers have redeployed Zach Merrett back into his customary role in the midfield over the past month, and he was typically busy. In what could be his final weeks at the club, the former skipper had 29 disposals and 401 metres gained.



Sam Durham was quiet, but rookies Dyson Sharp, who found plenty of the ball, and Jacob Farrow, with two goals, continued their development. The Bombers host the Swans next Sunday, and could yet pinch one more victory, at home against Port Adelaide, to close what has been a largely dismal campaign. Keep up to date with the best AFL coverage in the country.

World.title: ‘Faceless’ foes to face off as Carlton and St Kilda scrap for wildcard spot
World.content:
Analysis SportAFLAFL 2026 ‘Faceless’ foes to face off as Carlton and St Kilda scrap for wildcard spot Peter Ryan August 8, 2026 — 8:36pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

There will be plenty of familiar faces on both sides when Carlton take on St Kilda at Marvel Stadium in what is arguably the most consequential clash between the two clubs since the 1972 preliminary final. Liam Stocker will be donning a Saints jumper for his 100th AFL game when he lines up alongside other ex-Blues Jack Silvagni and Tom De Koning, while former Saint Blake Acres will wear the No.13 Carlton jumper Stocker wore in his 28 matches with Carlton. Another win under interim coach Josh Fraser will kick the Blues two games clear of St Kilda in the race for a wildcard spot, while Ross Lyon’s team will leapfrog Carlton if they win – with a softer draw in their remaining two matches likely to see them home. St Kilda stars Tom De Koning and Jack Silvagni were huge names at Carlton before leaving the Blues as free agents. Getty Images It’s a huge game, particularly so for the Saints, who grabbed Carlton free agents De Koning and Silvagni during last year’s trade period to set them on a course for finals.



However, the animosity that existed between the two clubs in recent years as former Carlton list manager and club great Stephen Silvagni grabbed players from the list after an acrimonious departure from the club at the end of 2019 is said to have dissipated. Sources from both clubs, and former club officials who wanted to remain anonymous in order to speak freely, said there was no longer any angst towards each other, with the regime at Carlton now different from the one in place when Silvagni, Jack’s father, departed. While the Blues fought off an attempt to poach Brodie Kemp at the end of 2024, and weren’t happy to lose De Koning to such an outrageous offer last season, Silvagni was not a player they tried desperately to retain, despite his name being synonymous with the club. Josh Fraser has led the Blues to a 9-2 record since taking over as interim coach. AFL Photos A minor skirmish earlier this year, when the clearance of Carlton VFL player Ethan Phillips to St Kilda’s VFL list took longer than necessary, also showed the clubs were happy to play the game hard.



But when the two teams line up on Sunday evening a rivalry will be the furthest thing from their minds. “Every week it is about a faceless opponent, everyone builds up who you are playing, [but] your biggest opponent is yourself,” Lyon said after Silvagni and De Koning played against their former club for the first time in round eight. The two clubs have shared 46 players over their history, with former Blues Jack Carroll and Paddy Dow still on the Saints’ list, but they have hardly built a rivalry. The two teams have played against each other in just five finals, with the ’72 preliminary final their most recent. The Saints’ winning record of 26.75 per cent over Carlton is their lowest winning rate against any side in their history. In the late-1980s they tried to reverse that, with the Carlton crew consisting of premiership Blues Alex Marcou, Peter McConville and Ken Sheldon joining St Kilda at the end of their careers alongside other Blues Spiro Kourkoumelis, Warren Jones and Ricky Nixon.



Carlton great Alex Jesaulenko ended his playing career at the Saints The Age They had joined soon after the most famous Blue to become a Saint, Alex Jesaulenko, controversially joined the club in 1980 after coaching Carlton to a flag as captain-coach in 1979. None of the moves worked for the Saints, who spent that decade languishing at the bottom while the Blues kept playing in grand finals at winning flags. But the arrival of Carlton’s Aaron Hamill at Moorabbin in 2001 began to reverse that winning record, particularly at Marvel Stadium. The Saints now lead the head-to-head battle at that venue 22-8, with their two-point win over Carlton in the final round of 2024 tipping the Blues out of finals momentarily before Port Adelaide beat Fremantle later that day.



They defeated them comfortably earlier this season when the Blues, then coached by Michael Voss, suffered a familiar second-half collapse and Jack Silvagni showed he was on the path to an outstanding season. Sunday night is different. Lyon noted during the week Fraser has improved Carlton’s defence by six goals and jokingly nominated him for coach of the year for his effort in turning the Blues around. Fraser, for his part, was not getting caught up in any suggestions this game was anything other than business as usual – a game to win against a faceless opponent who had a talented bloke wearing No.7 (Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera) they had to worry about. “These are the games you want to play in,” Fraser said.



“These are the opportunities you want to be afforded. We’ve done enough to this point to have the opportunity to play in a game like this. We’ll lean into it, but it won’t be about the outcome – it’ll be the brand of football we want to play,” Fraser said. Nothing about the opposition. Nothing about the want to defeat the mob that contains a few of their former players. The process – that’s what Ross and Josh will focus on.

World.title: Buyer pays $2.91m for inner west semi for kids to live in while at uni
World.content:
PropertyNewsAuctions Buyer pays $2.91m for inner west semi for kids to live in while at uni Robyn Willis Updated August 8, 2026 — 8:32pm ,first published 1:08pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

A two-storey Erskineville semi sold for $2.91 million at auction on Saturday to an overseas buyer who the selling agent said had purchased it for his children to live in while studying at university. About 30 people, including several neighbours, gathered in the open-plan living area at the rear of 59A Prospect Street to witness the auction of the four-bedroom, three-bathroom architecturally designed home. The property had a guide of $2.5 million and sold for $260,000 above the reserve of $2.65 million. There is no legal requirement for a vendor’s reserve to be in line with their property’s price guide.



Six parties registered to bid, with bidding opening at $2.52 million. Two parties initially battled it out in increments of $10,000, $20,000 and $30,000. When bidding reached $2.65 million, two new bidders entered the fray, with 15 bid increases of similar sizes going back and forth between the two. A final bid of $5000 ended the spectacle with the underbidders, a couple with a child who own a property further west but rent locally, quietly saying “I think we’re out”. It was socks all round for the auction of 9A Prospect Road as a crowd assembled in the compact open-plan living area. James Brickwood A lawyer acting on behalf of the successful bidder said his client was based overseas. Records show the property on the 144-square-metre site last sold in 2016 for $1.92 million. The property was one of 520 scheduled to go to auction in Sydney this week. By evening, Domain Group recorded a preliminary auction clearance rate of 50 per cent from 292 reported results throughout the week, while 94 auctions were withdrawn.





The landscaped backyard at the rear of 59A Prospect Street. Domain One of the vendors, who was present at the auction, said that while it was “very difficult to move” because her family had enjoyed the close-knit local community, an “outstanding” property closer to the city had convinced them to make a fresh start, so they bought it. In Lane Cove, a local family with a young child paid $1,463,000 for a three-bedroom apartment after it passed in at auction on Saturday. Bidding for the property at 2/15 Longueville Road opened at $1.38 million, increasing in bids of $10,000 to reach $1.45 million when things stalled and it passed in. The lead bidder was then invited to increase their offer and, after half an hour of negotiating, the property sold.



The apartment had a guide of $1.4 million and a reserve of $1.5 million. Related Article Sydney house prices ‘Fewer buyers’: The Sydney suburbs with the deepest property downturns Two bidders registered, although Raine & Horne Lower North Shore sales agent Oscar Nicholls was initially expecting only one. The underbidder was an investor who had seen the property once early in the campaign and was attracted to it for its yield potential, Nicholls said. “He got to a point [in the bidding] and said ‘at this price point it doesn’t make any sense’. He has a couple of investments which he is holding because rents are up,” Nicholls said. The vendor was a single-parent family who bought a four-bedroom home. Nicholls said market conditions were good for upsizers.



“She got a really good deal on what she bought,” he said of the new property. The three-bedroom apartment has two bathrooms, a double garage and a living area opening onto a private courtyard. Domain In Bondi Junction, negotiations continued after a two-bedroom art deco apartment passed in at $775,000. Two parties registered to bid for 2/143 Old South Head Road but just a single bid of $750,000 was placed when the auction opened. The lead bidder, a first home buyer renting in Paddington, was invited to advance on their offer with a further bid of $775,000 before the property passed in.



The apartment, sold as a deceased estate, had a guide of $800,0000 and a reserve of $850,000. It is one of nine apartments in a block positioned between Bellevue Hill and Bondi Junction and features high ornate ceilings, timber fretwork and picture rails, typical of the era. The art deco apartment is one of just nine in the boutique block. Domain A sales agent for Ray White Eastern Beaches, Angus Gorrie, expects the property to sell next week. “It takes a bit more time [to sell in this market], but we had two registered buyers, and we are getting close,” he said. “People are out there – the market is better than it was in June.”
